articles.title: Who is Alexia Putellas? All you need to know about Spain's three-time Ballon d'Or winner
articles.summary: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for a record-equalling third time on Monday after an impressive 2025-26 season with Barcelona.
articles.body: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for a record-equalling third time on Monday after an impressive 2025-26 season with Barcelona.The 32-year-old helped Barcelona win four trophies, including the Women's Champions League, before leaving her childhood club to join Women's Super League (WSL) side London City Lionesses in July.Putellas also played a key role in Spain's success in the Women's Nations League last December. Her latest award puts her alongside former Barcelona teammate Aitana Bonmati, who won the honour in 2023, 2024 and 2025.Putellas had previously claimed the award in 2021 and 2022. Her latest victory marks a remarkable comeback after a serious knee injury threatened to derail her career.Who is Alexia Putellas?Born in Mollet del Valles, a town near Barcelona in Spain's Catalonia region, Putellas grew up playing football on the streets. She soon became a Barcelona fan and regularly watched matches at Camp Nou.She admired former Barcelona and Spain midfielder Andres Iniesta, along with Brazilian stars Rivaldo and Ronaldinho. Her early football journey included a summer camp run by former Barcelona midfielder Xavi and spells with local club CE Sabadell.Putellas later joined Barcelona's famous La Masia academy for a year before moving to Espanyol and Levante. She returned to Barcelona in 2012, beginning a long association with the club she had supported since childhood.During her 14 years at Barcelona, she won 38 trophies, including 10 league titles and four European Cups. She also earned the nickname 'La Reina', which means 'The Queen'.Putellas first won the Ballon d'Or Feminin in 2021 and successfully defended the award in 2022. However, her career suffered a major setback when she tore her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) just before the European Championship that year. The injury ruled her out of the tournament and kept her away from her best form for some time. Although she won the Ballon d'Or again in 2022, she had a limited role in Spain's 2023 Women's World Cup-winning campaign.Putellas gradually returned to her best. She scored in the 2024 Women's Champions League final and continued to improve the following season.In 2025-26, she took on greater responsibility in Barcelona's attack while Bonmati was sidelined for five months with an injury. Putellas helped the club win four trophies and finished the campaign with 21 goals and 13 assists across all competitions.She also scored twice in Spain's 4-0 victory over England in June, a result that secured Spain's place at the 2027 Women's World Cup.What did Putellas say after winning her third Ballon d'Or?Putellas used her latest success to encourage young players around the world to follow their dreams, regardless of their gender or background."All the boys and girls around the world - if you love football and if you want to play football, play football. It doesn't matter if you're a boy or if you're a girl," Putellas said as quoted by BBC."Doesn't matter where you come from. Don't listen if someone tells you, you can't do it. Believe in yourself."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: El último truco del Mago Pop: el CD Cieza tiene magia en la Copa
articles.standfirst: El ilusionista y su primo Antonio, el presidente, se hicieron con el club murciano hace unos años y esta temporada, otra vez, se han ganado la opción de jugar la Copa del Rey
articles.summary: El ilusionista y su primo Antonio, el presidente, se hicieron con el club murciano hace unos años y esta temporada, otra vez, se han ganado la opción de jugar la Copa del Rey
articles.body: La Copa siempre llega cargada de magia. Campos imposibles, vestuarios alejados del lujo, jugadores que trabajan de panaderos o electricistas... fútbol en esencia. En el caso del Club Deportivo Cieza, equipo de segunda RFEF de la provincia de Murcia, lo de la magia no es una forma de hablar. Desde hace ya unos años, poco antes de la pandemia, los primos Antonio Díaz Sánchez y Antonio Díaz Cascajosa se hicieron con la propiedad del club. Les doy más detalles. El segundo de los Antonino Díaz es el artista, mago, ilusionista, más taquillero del mundo. Sí, es el Mago Pop. Junto a su primo decidió cumplir uno de sus sueños: tener un equipo de fútbol. Y fueron a la raíz. La familia tiene origen en Murcia. Sus padres nacieron en Santomera y vivieron mucho tiempo en Cieza antes de emigrar a Cataluña. "Siempre hemos sido muy futboleros... y del Barça", comenta el Antonio presidente a MARCA sobre el césped artificial del campo de la Arboleja. De hecho el Mago Pop no se perdió el domingo el Clásico en el Camp Nou. La Arboleja es uno de esos estadios que huelen a Copa, este miércoles estrenan iluminación fija que la pasada campaña les tocó poner grúas de luz portátiles para que se pudiera ver bien el partido por televisión, con unas vistas de la montaña de la Atalaya que a uno le reconfortan con el fútbol. Este miércoles les visita el Granada, meterán cerca de 3.000 aficionados, porque otro año más se han ganado el premio de jugar el torneo del K.O. La pasada edición se cargaron al Córdona y el Levante sudó tinta para seguir vivo. Desde que el Mago Pop y su primo tomaran el control han sumado dos ascensos y su estreno en Segunda RFEF está siendo brillante. "Antonio ha venido un par de veces y seguro que este año cuando acabe la gira estará aquí con el equipo. Le encanta estar pendiente", cuenta su primo que trabaja en la empresa de espectáculos que al mismo tiempo que ha comprado un equipo de fútbol ha adquirido tres teatros en Barcelona. "Hay veces que si jugamos y tiene función hasta pregunta por el pinganillo cómo va el equipo", comenta el presidente al que los jugadores ya le aprietan con alguna prima especial si esta temporada hay número de ilusionismo en la Copa. "Hemos hablado de ir todos en Navidad a Barcelona a ver uno de sus espectáculos y pasar un tiempo con él", al 'Primo Pop' se le cae el fútbol por los bolsillos. Jugó en las categorías inferiores del Murcia, más tarde en el Manlleu y cuentan de él que marcaba goles a porrillo. "Voy cada dos semanas a Barcelona para hablar con Antonio y muchos días acabamos hablando de fútbol, del equipo, de los planes de futuro...". Y mira que tienen cosas de las que hablar porque la carrera del Mago Pop es imparable. Se viene un Bernabéu en lo que puede ser el espectáculo de magia e ilusionismo más espectacular de la historia. Con un presupuesto de algo más de un millón de euros, el Cieza sigue creciendo año a año. Esta temporada, pese al ascenso, el presidente decidió cambiar al entrenador y el nuevo míster, José Miguel Campos, curtido en mil batallas, ha sido un acierto. Domina la categoría y eso se nota en un equipo recién ascendido. Antes de atender a MARCA los chicos tienen charla del presidente. La victoria del fin de se mana con tres goles de Piti, los tres de penalti, aún colea. Edu Luna es el capitán que los manda, el central es uno de los veteranos de la plantilla. "Tenemos un respaldo y una figura importante como el Mago Pop y sentimos su apoyo. Su primo Antonio está en el día a día con nosotros y eso hay que valorarlo. Tenemos magia en la Alboreja y en Cieza. Tenemos un campo algo reducido y nos da algo de ventaja y para cualquiera será complicado ganarnos". El capi marca el camino de un equipo que tiene una pinta tremenda. Tras la sesión de trabajo y la charla con el presidente, todos se citan para hablar de primas después del partido ante el Granada y las bromas se disparan en cuanto el presi decreta el 'rompan filas'. Foto de equipo y a centrarse en seguir avanzando. Que la Copa tenía magia ya lo sabíamos, pero que haya un equipo 'mágico' en la Copa es otro nivel.

articles.title: Arsenal should unleash Max Dowman, Liverpool and Chelsea clash in battle of the Basques and Man City continue defence - Carabao Cup talking points
articles.summary: Watch every match from the Carabao Cup fourth round live on Sky Sports; watch in-game clips and FREE match highlights across Sky Sports' digital platforms; Fleetwood Town vs Arsenal live on Sky Sports Football on Tuesday; Liverpool vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports Main Event on Wednesday
articles.body:
It's time for Mikel Arteta to unleash Max Dowman regularly for Arsenal.

The talented 16-year-old is hardly the new kid on the block anymore. In the last round of the Carabao Cup, Dowman dazzled against Ipswich Town with a man-of-the-match display and is expected to be the creative fulcrum of the Arsenal attack again against Fleetwood Town.

But having largely been held back by Arteta this season, here comes the teenager's first real chance since his breakthrough to become an Arsenal regular.

The point where Arteta releases the shackles off Dowman and puts him in as one of his key stars is an important moment not just for Arsenal, but for English football as well. This is a diamond player, a rare gem that eventually needs to shine.

With all the Ballon d'Or talk this week, it is worth remembering that Lamine Yamal was unleashed by both Barcelona and Spain without hesitation. Does Dowman need that same treatment?

Bukayo Saka's injury has opened the door now for Dowman to play week in, week out for Arsenal. But not just as a rotational option, Dowman could really challenge Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze for a starting spot, given the pair are yet to show the consistency required since joining Arsenal.

Is this the period where Dowman's career accelerates? Sam Blitz

Savage's Posh revival faces stern Bradford test

Robbie Savage is slowly turning Peterborough United around, and now has the chance to make some history.

The former Wales and Leicester City midfielder left National League club Forest Green Rovers in early October to join the struggling League One side, and has taken five points from his first four games in charge.

He promised attacking football, and Posh have scored seven goals since.

To reach the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 1992, they must unlock a watertight Bradford City defence that has conceded just five times in 12 league games.

Under new boss Michael Duff, who took over from Graham Alexander just four days after Savage was appointed, Bradford haven't conceded a goal in four matches, but three have ended 0-0. They have netted just 10 times in League One this season, yet sit third.

Bradford, finalists in 2013, are attempting to boost the attendance by offering tickets for just £5, setting the stage for a bumper crowd as they look to keep their own cup hopes alive. David Richardson

In the battle of the Basques, how strong will Iraola and Alonso go?

It will be intriguing to see just how strong Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso go with their lineups at Anfield on Wednesday night, with both Basques facing huge Premier League games on the weekend, albeit for different reasons.

Liverpool are currently in the middle of a run of four home games in a row and will head into the Chelsea clash bouncing after three straight wins, so will the Reds head coach look to prioritise the visit of champions Arsenal to Anfield on Super Sunday , or would another victory help maintain the feelgood factor around the club right now?

Either way, one player certain to start the tie against the club he began his career at is young Reds forward Rio Ngumoha, who shone against Villarreal in the Champions League last week, before playing the final 13 minutes of Sunday's 2-0 win against Brighton.

As for the visitors, Alonso will be looking for a reaction from his players after Saturday's "awful" 2-0 loss to Tottenham, as Gary Neville described their display at the Bridge. But, again, where will the Chelsea manager's priorities lie with hugely important league games against Man Utd, Sunderland and Leeds on the horizon?

Alonso, who will be without the suspended Cole Palmer after his sending off against Spurs, will surely want to freshen things up at Anfield, but as Paul Merson told Sky Sports : "If they get beat by Liverpool and Man Utd this week, then Chelsea are in big trouble. You'd be seriously thinking they'd be lucky to get Champions League this season. And that can't happen. Whatever happens, that can't happen." Rich Morgan

Man City-Brighton double-header presents big chance for Hurzeler

Manchester City and Brighton meet twice this week, once in the cup and once in the league. It's a chance for Fabian Hurzeler to prove that Brighton can consistently mix it with the best teams in the division after faltering at Liverpool at the weekend.

For all the club's progress, and the never-ending stream of compliments about Hurzeler's progressive style of play, he is missing the tangible evidence to cement Brighton as the Premier League's great disruptors. The EFL Cup presents the perfect opportunity to do that.

Brighton are unbeaten in four games against Man City (W2, D2) - their best ever run against such usually-dominant opposition. Hurzeler's brand of high-intensity football is exactly the style City tend to find most unsettling, so the visitors should arrive to the Etihad full of confidence.

They're perfectly capable of causing an upset to dispatch of the holders. Laura Hunter

Europe has helped, not hindered - but can Villa and Bournemouth also balance cup run?

Europe is usually viewed as a hindrance to domestic form, but it has been a positive thus far for Aston Villa and Bournemouth.

Both teams started slowly this season. Villa had not scored a goal in the Premier League until the 2-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest on September 12, while their first league win came a week later at Tottenham.

Unai Emery's men kicked into gear with a 3-2 win against Club Brugge earlier in September and have now gone seven games unbeaten across all competitions since beating Coventry City in the last round of the Carabao Cup.

Bournemouth are a similar story. It was a slow start under Marco Rose, but their performances in the Europa League have ignited the new era.

They had to wait until October 18 for a first win in the top flight but they now come into this game against Villa full of confidence after beating AC Milan and Manchester United across a four-game winning streak.

After starting slowly, the two teams are beginning to flex their muscles and are showcasing why they are regarded as two of the best run clubs in the division. However, how they balance this Carabao Cup tie will be the ultimate test for their squad depth.

Can they juggle European football, the priority that is the Premier League and a cup run? We'll find out on Wednesday. Patrick Rowe

Fulham finding form as Palace and Sage face Carabao Cup reckoning

When Fulham and Crystal Palace first met in early September, both managers were under pressure after losing their opening two Premier League games. Ahead of Wednesday's Carabao Cup meeting, however, the balance of power has shifted dramatically.

Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham have found momentum at precisely the right time, winning back-to-back league games against Hull and Coventry.

Oscar Bobb's late winner at the CBS Arena was another sign of a side growing in resilience, while consecutive clean sheets suggest they are beginning to find the defensive stability that eluded them earlier in the season.

The crisis has not disappeared, but Arbeloa has bought himself breathing room via 'Arbeloa-ball'.

Pierre Sage, meanwhile, is facing an altogether different reckoning at Palace.

Consecutive defeats to Brighton and Newcastle, conceding seven goals without reply, have exposed a team desperately short of defensive organisation and confidence.

Palace have shipped 19 league goals, the division's worst record, and Sage's insistence that the problems are not tactical will do little to silence the growing discontent among supporters.

Wednesday offers Fulham a chance to deepen Palace's crisis. For Sage, it risks becoming another step towards the exit. William Bitibiri

Given their contrasting form this season, Brentford will be confident heading to the Stadium of Light this week. Not only that, they also have a decent pedigree in recent Carabao Cup campaigns.

They have reached the quarter-finals in three of the last five seasons, including the last two - and were knocked out by the eventual winners in 2024/25 (Newcastle) and 2025/26 (Man City). Finalists Chelsea knocked them out in their other quarter-final appearance in 2021/22.

Of course, Keith Andrews will be hoping to go one better this season - but they have Sunderland to beat first.

The Black Cats have been eliminated in six of their last eight League Cup fourth round ties - the most recent in 2021/22 - and are struggling to find the magic touch they had last season.

But form doesn't always translate onto the pitch and knockout football is a different beast altogether. At home, Sunderland will feel they are a match for anyone - and will not want to get stung again on Wednesday. Charlotte Marsh

Can Toffees or Magpies lay down a marker before PL rematch?

The Carabao Cup often gives teams a chance to rotate their squad in order to remain fresh for the upcoming Premier League games. That is less likely to be the case here. Instead, it could act as a preview of their league meeting on Monday night.

Everton’s paper-thin squad has already been rocked by the illness of Jack Grealish and the concussion of Jarrad Branthwaite. Whether he likes it or not, David Moyes will have to go to the well with the exact same group and just pray for no more knocks.

Newcastle’s options have also been rather depleted, but they do have the advantage when it comes to strength in depth, aided greatly by the return of Anthony Elanga during the league win over Crystal Palace.

The thirst for silverware on Tyneside may encourage Matthias Jaissle to put out a relatively strong team as the Magpies look to regain the title they won two years' ago under Eddie Howe.

If these two do line up strongly, then perhaps as important as progression in the cup is the opportunity to lay down a marker before they meet again on Merseyside a mere 96 hours later. Callum Bishop

articles.title: Roberto Gómez avisa a Lamine Yamal y Mbappé tras perder el Balón de Oro: "Les va a pasar una factura terrible"
articles.standfirst: El periodista compara la situación de ambos futbolistas con la de Vinicius y critica sus campañas antes de la gala
articles.summary: El periodista compara la situación de ambos futbolistas con la de Vinicius y critica sus campañas antes de la gala
articles.body: La victoria de Harry Kane en el Balón de Oro 2026 sigue dando mucho que hablar. El delantero inglés se impuso a Lamine Yamal y Kylian Mbappé en una gala que ha analizado Roberto Gómez en La Tribu de Radio MARCA, donde ha advertido de las consecuencias que puede tener para ambos futbolistas no haber conseguido el galardón. "Les va a pasar factura a Mbappé y a Lamine este Balón de Oro", ha asegurado Roberto Gómez durante su conversación con Raúl Varela. El periodista se ha mostrado especialmente crítico con las apariciones públicas de ambos candidatos durante los meses previos a la gala: "Han estado mendigando los dos". "Han estado mendigando entrevistas para acá, entrevistas para allá y les va a pasar factura", ha insistido el periodista, que considera que los dos futbolistas estaban convencidos de sus posibilidades de ganar el premio. Para explicar su postura, Roberto Gómez ha recurrido al ejemplo de Vinicius. "Como le pasó a Vinicius, hay un Vinicius antes y un Vinicius después del Balón de Oro", ha afirmado. Y ha añadido: "Le marcó y le va a marcar toda su vida y le va a marcar tanto a Mbappé como a Lamine". El periodista cree que esta situación podría afectar a los dos jugadores, especialmente en los estadios rivales. "Les va a pasar una factura terrible que indudablemente les va a afectar a partir de ahora", ha advertido. Sin embargo, Gómez también ha reconocido el fenómeno que representa Lamine Yamal entre los aficionados españoles. "Yo estoy harto de ver en Madrid a niños, niñas, pequeñas, mayores, con la camiseta de Lamine, que eso no lo había visto yo en mi vida", ha destacado.

articles.title: Harry Kane becomes first Englishman in 25 years to win Ballon d’Or award
articles.summary: Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the prestigious Ballon d’Or award thanks to his prolific scoring last season.
articles.body: LONDON — Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the prestigious Ballon d’Or award on Monday thanks to his prolific scoring last season. Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last campaign — he was Europe’s top scorer — and smashed scoring records in Germany for Bayern Munich and at the World Cup, where he captained England to a third-place finish. The 33-year-old Kane says winning the prestigious individual award was built on so much more. “Anything is possible with hard work, when no one else is watching, to go through the ups and downs, to learn through resilience, determination and self-belief,” an emotional Kane said in a message to young players, after reflecting on his early career struggles. “My journey wasn’t straightforward. I wasn’t the kid who went straight to the top. I had to experience the downs,” he added. “I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration as well.” Kane was followed in the voting by Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal — voted best young talent for a third straight year — 2024 winner Rodri and record eight-time winner Lionel Messi. Kane thanked his teammates, coaches, parents, children — “It’s past your bedtime” — and wife Kate, “my best friend. We’ve been through ups and downs for sure. You’re my biggest supporter. You always want the best for me.” Kane led Bayern to the Bundesliga and German Cup double, scoring a hat trick against Stuttgart in the cup final. Bayern also reached the Champions League semifinals. At the World Cup, he scored six times to pass Gary Lineker as England’s all-time leading World Cup scorer and placed himself among the all-time top five in tournament history. His lineup lost to Argentina in the semifinals but beat Mbappé’s France for third place, England’s best World Cup placing in 60 years. An Englishman hadn’t won the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001. “It’s massive for England, for our country. (The ceremony) being here in London was a good omen for me,” Kane said. “It’s been too long. Certainly (there have been) incredible English players... To put us back on the map, to put us here with this trophy I’m extremely proud. Playing for England is my biggest honor, the thing I love to do the most.” England coach Thomas Tuchel told Kane the Three Lions are “lucky to have you as our leader.” “I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognized by the football world,” Tuchel said. Fans packed the streets and climbed light poles near the London Palladium, where the event was held, for a glimpse of the arriving athletes. Kane stopped to sign autographs on his way in. They stayed through the ceremony and chanted Kane’s name as he left the theater near Oxford Circus after midnight. Kane planned to celebrate with family and friends, but just a little. “We have a cup game on Wednesday so it can’t get too messy,” Kane said, noting he has an early Tuesday flight back to Munich in time for team training. Monday’s ceremony was held in London for the first time in recognition of the inaugural winner 70 years ago, England’s Stanley Matthews in 1956. Putellas hat trick of awards Earlier, Spain star Alexia Putellas won her record-equaling third women’s Ballon d’Or after leading her former club Barcelona to multiple trophies last season including the Women’s Champions League. Putellas, who joined London City Lionesses in the offseason, also helped Spain win the Women’s Nations League last December. The 32-year-old midfielder ended Spain teammate Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign. Putellas won the prestigious award in 2021 and 2022, tore her ACL and saw Bonmati rise to stardom. Bonmati, who completed her women’s Ballon d’Or three-peat in 2025, was not on this year’s shortlist after breaking her leg in December. There wasn’t a women’s Ballon d’Or until 2018, when Ada Hegerberg won it. Putellas urged young players to approach the sport with “love and passion.” “Believe in yourself, that’s the most important thing,” she said. “If you have a dream, go for it, even if at some point you have to start from zero.” Putellas had joined Barcelona in 2012 and called her time at the Catalan club “something special.” “I’m really grateful for having 14 seasons as a player (at Barcelona),” she said. “What I experienced last year was like a perfect story.”

articles.title: Decano contra barrio
articles.standfirst: El Recreativo de Huelva se medirá al Rayo Vallecano en la primera ronda de la Copa del Rey
articles.summary: El Recreativo de Huelva se medirá al Rayo Vallecano en la primera ronda de la Copa del Rey
articles.body: Ante ustedes, el decano del fútbol español. El Rayo Vallecano se enfrentará en su primera ronda de la Copa del Rey al Recreativo de Huelva. El equipo más antiguo del fútbol español, con 137 primaveras que cumplirá el próximo 18 de diciembre. Ambos se vieron las caras por primera vez en Segunda, para después enfrentarse en Primera y también en la Copa del Rey. El sorteo ha deparado que se vean las caras, 16 años después. La última vez que jugaron fue en la temporada 2010/11 en la división de plata. El resultado de ambos encuentros quedó en tablas. Primero, empate a cero en Vallecas; después, a uno en el Nuevo Colombino. Aquella campaña tiene ciertas similitudes con la que estamos viviendo actualmente en cuanto a la situación extradeportiva del Rayo Vallecano. Esta temporada, la Comunidad de Madrid se ha visto obligada a cerrar el Estadio de Vallecas porque no cumplía con las medidas de seguridad. Hace 16 años, el club también estuvo en ruinas. El 17 de febrero de 2011, Ruiz Mateos anunció la salida del Rayo Vallecano a un concurso de acreedores porque Nueva Rumasa (propietaria del club) se había arruinado. Por aquel entonces, todo el personal que formaba parte del club dejó de cobrar. Una plantilla capitaneada por Míchel Sánchez (actual técnico del Ajax) y cuya portería la ocupaba David Cobeño, director deportivo en estos momentos. Formaban parte de ella otros mitos como Óscar Trejo, Amaya, Armenteros o Piti. Todos ellos dirigidos por José Ramón Sandoval. En la temporada 2009/10, el Rayo le endosó un 4-0 al Recreativo de Huelva en Vallecas. Aquella goleada certificó la permanencia de los primeros y quien abrió la lata fue Rubén Castro, máximo goleador de la historia del Real Betis. Este fue el último partido de Felipe Miñambres como entrenador, antes de pasar a la dirección deportiva del club. Antes de este duelo, en 1988, se produjo el resultado más abultado entre ambos clubes. Un 5-1, a favor del cuadro rayista. La mayor goleada a manos de los onubenses fue un 3-1 que se repitió en tres ocasiones. La primera de ellas en 1967 cuando a la Copa del Rey se le denominaba Copa del Generalísimo. En la primera vuelta de LaLiga 02/03, el Recre se impuso por 2-1 con goles de Xisco Muñoz y Loren que remontaron el tanto inicial de Ramón De Quintana. La vuelta tuvo lugar en la jornada 38 y el encuentro quedó empatado. Los dos colistas no tenían opción de salvarse y optaron por un pacto de no agresión, despidiéndose de Primera sin goles marcados y encajados en el último partido. El Recreativo de Huelva llega a su primer enfrentamiento de la Copa del Rey siendo el líder del Grupo 4 de Segunda Federación. Está en un excelente estado de forma, anotándole 5-0 al colista y tan solo ha perdido un encuentro esta temporada. El Rayo, por otra parte, viene de realizar su “peor partido de la temporada” (tal y como afirmó Beñat San José) ante el Elche y aunque la situación con la afición se haya relajado relativamente, la ruptura con la directiva parece imposible de reconducir. Esta semana, las Peñas han convocado una reunión con la dirección del equipo y en el caso de que no se produzca antes del sábado, el partido ante el Celta podría correr serio peligro. El club franjirrojo recorrerá más de 400 kilómetros para verse las caras con el ‘padre’ del fútbol español. La Copa mola en Vallecas y el camino comienza por Huelva.

articles.title: Un portal deportivo chino borra el nombre de Mbappé de la lista del Balón de Oro: "No existe tal persona"
articles.standfirst: Reemplazó el nombre de Mbappé por la expresión china 'chá wú cǐ rén', que significa "no existe tal persona" o "persona no encontrada"
articles.summary: Reemplazó el nombre de Mbappé por la expresión china 'chá wú cǐ rén', que significa "no existe tal persona" o "persona no encontrada"
articles.body: El portal deportivo chino Dongqiudi sustituyó el nombre de Kylian Mbappé por la expresión "no existe tal persona" en la clasificación del Balón de Oro de 2026, en la que el delantero del Real Madrid terminó segundo, tras la polémica por unas declaraciones sobre un 'meme' que lo compara con Mao Zedong. En la lista publicada este martes, el medio identificó al ganador, el inglés Harry Kane, y al tercer clasificado, el español Lamine Yamal, pero reemplazó el nombre del francés por la expresión china 'chá wú cǐ rén', que significa "no existe tal persona" o "persona no encontrada". Dongqiudi, una de las principales plataformas digitales especializadas en fútbol de China, también publicó una fotografía en blanco y negro de Mbappé, un tratamiento visual que en las redes sociales chinas suele asociarse con imágenes de personas fallecidas. El portal había difundido el lunes un comunicado en el que calificó de "inaceptables" las declaraciones del futbolista y aseguró que no las traduciría por considerar que perjudicaban los sentimientos de los aficionados y del pueblo chino. La controversia comenzó después de que Mbappé afirmara en una entrevista que uno de los 'memes' que más le divertían mostraba su rostro sobre el de un "dictador chino", aunque no mencionó expresamente a Mao. La polémica provocó este martes la ruptura de los acuerdos comerciales de Mbappé con las empresas chinas Dongpeng, Mengniu y Milkground, mientras que el Ministerio chino de Exteriores advirtió de que las palabras y los actos que "hieren los sentimientos del pueblo chino serán rechazados por todos los sectores de la sociedad". La televisión estatal CCTV suspendió las retransmisiones de LaLiga, según informó The Paper citando fuentes de la radiotelevisión pública, mientras que la plataforma Xiaohongshu (RedNote) impide seguir la cuenta del futbolista, como pudo comprobar EFE, y anunció la retirada de contenidos relacionados con él, aunque aclaró que su colaboración comercial había terminado en 2024

articles.title: Vivimos la fiesta de Harry Kane: "Es un delantero histórico para el fútbol"
articles.standfirst: La celebración por el trofeo ganado por el inglés se trasladó a un club de Londres
articles.summary: La celebración por el trofeo ganado por el inglés se trasladó a un club de Londres
articles.body: La fiesta por la conquista del Balón de Oro de Harry Kane se trasladó anoche a Amazónico, un club privado cerca del Teatro Palladium de Londres, donde el delantero del Bayern conquistó su primer galardón de este tipo con 33 años. Allí estaban gran parte de su familia, su doctor deportivo, el español Alejandro Elorriaga, algunos compañeros del Bayern como Olise, y otros grandes amigos del fútbol, como Ben Davies o Maddison, excompañeros de HK en el Tottenham, club en el que el actual Balón de Oro no conquistó ningún título. En Amazónico, todos cacareaban las virtudes profesionales, de resiliencia tras muchos años de carrera sin ganar y la categoría personal de un Harry que mostraba con humildad su preciado trofeo. "Es un delantero histórico para el fútbol", decía uno de sus amigos mientras mostraba orgulloso el Balón de Oro. Harry se convierte en el quinto jugador de la historia en conseguir en el mismo año Balón de Oro y Bota de Oro, algo que sólo han logrado Lionel Messi (2010, 2012 y 2019), Cristiano Ronaldo (2008 y 2014), Ronaldo Nazario (1997) y Gerd Müller (1970). HK, que está a punto de renovar su contrato con el Bayern hasta 2029, se preparará desde hoy para el 'Klasikker' ante el Borussia Dortmund del próximo sábado. Será el desafío para el capitán de la Selección inglesa que ayer engalanó alguno de los edificios emblemáticos de Londres con la imagen de su ya icónico Balón de Oro.

articles.title: Ricardo Sierra compara a Harry Kane con Benzema: "Es lo más parecido desde que se fue"
articles.standfirst: El periodista destaca la capacidad del delantero inglés para participar en el juego colectivo, mientras Pipi Estrada celebra que "no ha ganado el marketing"
articles.summary: El periodista destaca la capacidad del delantero inglés para participar en el juego colectivo, mientras Pipi Estrada celebra que "no ha ganado el marketing"
articles.body: Ricardo Sierra, Látigo Serrano, Nacho Palencia, Pipi Estrada Fernando Kallás y Nacho Labarga han sido los tertulianos de este martes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta semana, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por la gala del Balón de Oro y el triunfo de Harry Kane. "Es lo más parecido a Benzema desde que se fue ", ha asegurado Ricardo Sierra, que ha destacado las cualidades del delantero del Bayern de Múnich más allá de su capacidad goleadora. "Es un tipo que baja mucho, que ayuda mucho, que en lo colectivo funciona mucho", ha explicado. El periodista también ha defendido la justicia del resultado, pese a reconocer que había varios candidatos con argumentos para llevarse el premio. "A mí me parece tremendamente justo", ha señalado, recordando que el inglés no había protagonizado una campaña mediática como la de otros aspirantes. Uno de los más críticos con las campañas previas al Balón de Oro ha sido Pipi Estrada. "A mí lo que me ha gustado es que no ha ganado el marketing", ha asegurado, cuestionando el protagonismo que habían adquirido Lamine Yamal y Mbappé durante las semanas anteriores a la gala. Ricardo Sierra ha coincidido en que los otros dos aspirantes alimentaron las expectativas sobre sus posibilidades de ganar. "Yo creo que la campaña se la han hecho ellos", ha señalado, antes de explicar que ambos aprovecharon sus entrevistas para intentar reforzar sus candidaturas. Por su parte, Fernando Kallás también ha elogiado al delantero inglés. "Yo creo que hoy en día el sinónimo, el gran ejemplo de lo que es un jugador que pone siempre el colectivo antes que el individual", ha afirmado. "Kane es más que un delantero, es un jugador que baja a marcar, que arma juego, que se entrega totalmente a la causa de su equipo, de su selección", ha añadido Kallás, que ha celebrado el reconocimiento al futbolista inglés. Los tertulianos también han destacado el protagonismo del fútbol español durante la gala. "Tenéis que estar muy, pero muy orgullosos del fútbol español, porque es una victoria del fútbol español", ha concluido Kallás.

articles.title: Fofana, un regalo del cielo
articles.standfirst: El francés, con tres asistencias y un gol, marca diferencias en el equipo de García Plaza
articles.summary: El francés, con tres asistencias y un gol, marca diferencias en el equipo de García Plaza
articles.body: Luis García Plaza le exige más a Youssouf Fofana. El técnico se rinde al talento del francés, pero no le regala los oídos. "De Fofana ya hemos hablado bastante. Es un jugador que está por encima. Aún así le está costando adaptarse a jugar de distinta manera. Está acostumbrado a jugar en equipos más dominantes y le ha costado llegar a los últimos minutos", comentó ayer tras la victoria frente a Osasuna con dos asistencias del centrocampista. El técnico madrileño ha armado un Luis García Plaza ha montado un Sevilla intenso, incómodo para el rival, ultracompetitivo y solidario, pero lo que aporta Fofana, incluso en un día 'malo', es diferencial. José Ignacio Navarro, director deportivo del Sevilla, se coronó en las horas finales del mercado firmando a un jugador inalcanzable para la economía del club blanquirrojo. El efecto causado por el mediocampista perteneciente al Milan, que llegó a Nervión una vez que se frustró su fichaje por el Olympique de Lyon, ha sido inmediato tanto en el césped como en la grada. Aunque destaca por su imponente físico, su lectura en la recuperación y su buen posicionamiento en el césped, también sabe cómo sumar en fase ofensiva. Ante Osasuna, dio las dos asistencias de los tantos de la victoria a Isaac Romero y Félix para sumar la quinta victoria de lo que va de curso. En sus 248 partidos como profesional entre el Estrasburgo, el Mónaco, el Milan y el Sevilla es la primera vez que reparte dos pases de gol en un mismo partido. También dio el pase a Isaac en su gol ante el Levante. El club, en su web oficial, recuerda también que en materia anotadora se estrenó como goleador en el partido frente al Barcelona en el Sánchez-Pizjuán. La temporada pasada en el Milan, Fofana anotó dos goles y repartió tres asistencias en 33 partidos, números que está muy cerca de igualar en tan solo siete encuentros como sevillista. Isaac, MVP del último partido ante Osasuna, fue generoso en su comparecencia tras el choque y señaló a su compañero de filas cuando fue cuestionado por su gol: "Me la ha dejado muy bien Fofa y no me lo he pensado, le he pegado como he podido". "Hemos construido una gran familia dentro del vestuario. Nos llevamos todos súper bien, somos chavales jóvenes casi todos. Hablé antes del partido con Peque, que si marcaba me iba al banquillo con ellos a celebrarlo", añadía. Es, como él mismo se definió en su presentación, un centrocampista "híbrido". En el doble pivote junto a Agoumé o por detrás del delantero, Fofana, se adapta a cada jugador y siempre tiene algo que decir. "Estoy muy contento, sinceramente, de que llegara esta oportunidad porque no podía soñar con algo mejor. Sinceramente, en mi situación en aquel momento, para mí era perfecto" Los regalos se disfrutan y el sevillismo lo hace con su nuevo ídolo.

articles.title: Way-Too-Early Contenders for the 2027 Men's Ballon d'Or
articles.summary: Harry Kane has done it!
articles.body:
The Bayern Munich and England striker was named the Men's Ballon d'Or winner on Monday, beating Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to the award that felt like it could have gone to any of the top three.

Football waits for nobody. Kane may still be celebrating, but it's time to see if he can do it again next season, and if not, who may snatch the crown from his clutches.

Let's start with Lamine Yamal. While he looked disappointed to miss out on the award on Monday night, the 19-year-old will be many onlookers' favourite to capture the biggest individual prize in the sport next year.

Realistically, he also has much of his career ahead of him to win it.

The three-time Young Talent award winner has started this season in ridiculous fashion. His 10 goals and 10 assists in 13 games across La Liga and the Champions League only tell part of the story, though.

He is undoubtedly a leader in excellent Barcelona and Spain teams, a player who demands the ball and seems capable of producing something incredible every time he's in possession.

Yamal is also a proponent of a dying art; one of those footballers who still tries stuff . That piece of skill against Galatasaray in the Champions League was not only remarkable for its creativity and execution, but it was also a reminder of how such flamboyancy has been drilled out of modern footballers.

The Closest Competition: Kane and Mbappe

In truth, next year's top three is likely to look very similar to this year's final list. Both Kylian Mbappe and Harry Kane should be considered Yamal's main threats once more—although one factor could weigh far heavier than it did in the 2026 voting: whoever wins the Champions League.

The 2026 vote was so hard to call because Paris Saint-Germain took the prize without an individual putting up the season Ousmane Dembele did the year before. The French team's highest-ranked player was Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who finished sixth. Neither looks set to challenge this year as things stand, with ongoing injury issues plaguing PSG's start to the season.

Real Madrid's inability to compete for the aforementioned club competition has harmed Mbappe's odds in recent times. He is electric, with a goalscoring output that is keeping Jose Mourinho's inconsistent side in the La Liga title race.

Mbappe's brace in El Clásico underlined the hunger of a man whom many expected to emerge as the leading Ballon d'Or contender after Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo's era of dominance. Those grittier goals will be just as important to his case as the spectacular ones, particularly if they return Los Blancos to some kind of domination in Spain or on the continent.

Kane doesn't have that issue—Bayern will remain German champions. His evolution from a consistent goalscorer into one of the world's best playmakers played a huge role in him being recognised this year. He nearly registered an assist directly from a goal-kick in the recent draw with Arsenal.

The England international isn't as flashy as Yamal or Mbappe, but his footballing IQ and ability to roam while maintaining influence are second to none. He may need Bayern to capture the Champions League to make it a repeat, though.

The Outsiders: Raphinha, Olise and Bellingham

Right now, it feels like certain teammates of next year's expected top three should be considered the outsiders to the throne.

Yamal's output directly links to that of Raphinha, whose stunning 2024-25 season somehow only landed him a fifth-place finish, when he really should have been considered top three at the very least.

The Brazilian criticised the voting system after that, then had an injury-ravaged 2025-26 season. He's thriving again—with 15 goals and three assists in 11 La Liga and Champions League games so far—but he needs to stay fit to have any chance. He looks the best of the rest as things stand.

Michael Olise may have something to say about that, though. His progression since moving to Bayern is nothing short of remarkable, summed up by 27 goals and 34 assists in 51 starts and 15 substitute appearances in the Bundesliga heading into this season. He's already on six goals and three assists in six starts as we move into November.

While Olise is spectacular, he suffers a bit from not being Bayern's bona fide, out-and-out main man. Each of the outsider picks arguably has one player ahead of them if you were ranking quality at their club alone.

Olise would need to seriously outperform Kane to finish above him. He's capable of doing it through his hard work and coverage of the pitch, but it seems a tough bet that he'd pick up more votes unless he were undeniable.

The same can be said for Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham, who should be considered further back than Olise in the overall chase. The 23-year-old is the beating heart of Madrid and England, a terrific match-winner who drives his team forward, but the presence of Mbappe at Madrid and Kane with England makes things complicated.

Does it seem strange to suggest Erling Haaland as a wild card?

Manchester City's goal machine finished eighth in the 2026 vote and already has 13 goals in 11 games this season. However, my gut is saying he could vastly outperform many of the players on this list and still not receive the support needed to lift the trophy.

The reasoning is twofold. Firstly, Haaland isn't an all-round player like many of those who finish above him. While he does contribute to buildup play more than people give him credit for, he's the finisher. He is quickly criticised when he doesn't score, with some questioning his value to the team if he's not consistently impacting the scoreline (which, so far this year, he is).

Then there's the uncertainty surrounding Manchester City. An independent commission found the club guilty of 114 of the 115 charges relating to Premier League financial rules, but City maintain their innocence and have appealed. Any potential sanctions remain to be determined.

How the case might affect Haaland's Ballon d'Or chances remains speculative. His individual performances will give voters plenty to weigh up regardless.

Realistically, beyond the Norway international, there are few others who fit into this category.

Dembele and Kvaratskhelia's recent injury issues may leave room for Desire Doue. Arsenal would simply have to win the Champions League for Declan Rice to be considered. Then there are players such as Rodri and Vitinha, who probably fall behind colleagues if their clubs win it all.

While not impossible, it would take something spectacular to oust any of this year's top three.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Rankings after Week 8
articles.summary: And here come the Hurricanes.
articles.body:
While superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith and Ohio State had a week off, Miami's standout duo of Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney narrowed the gap in the 2026 Heisman Trophy race.

Behind them is an intriguing, ever-rotating cast of candidates that includes some big-name players, an ascending QB and a true freshman wideout.

Although the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss (+3000)

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State (+4000)

Braden Atkinson, QB, Oregon State (+10000)

Noah Fifita, QB, Arizona : Week 9 is the moment for Fifita to demand a place in the conversation as 6-1 Arizona heads to Texas Tech. Right now, he lacks a signature game. But if the Cats win, Fifita's numbers—2,186 offensive yards and 21 total scores—would support his legitimacy.

Sam Leavitt, QB, LSU : Attrition has provided a second life for Leavitt, who faded from the Heisman radar because of a turnover-plagued start. However, he's totaled 2,487 yards and 25 touchdowns for 6-2 LSU. After an open weekend to end October, the Tigers face a gauntlet that includes Alabama, Texas and Tennessee.

Kenny Minchey, QB, Kentucky : As long as Kentucky keeps rolling, Minchey will hang around. He put up a modest line in the recent win over Vanderbilt, managing 226 total yards and two scores, but UK is now 7-1 entering its open week.

Devon Dampier, QB, Utah : It feels similar for Dampier and 7-0 Utah. Despite throwing two interceptions against Houston, he managed 204 yards through the air, with 150 yards and two touchdowns on the ground in a 21-13 escape. Dampier and the Utes travel to Cincinnati this weekend.

Michael Hawkins Jr., QB, West Virginia : Hawkins has shredded box scores all season for 5-3 West Virginia. While passing for 1,598 yards and 11 scores, he's scampered for 836 yards and an FBS-high 16 touchdowns. Hawkins' margin for error is thin, as team success has historically mattered. The Mountaineers have a brutal November ahead, but this production is gaudy.

Gunner Stockton, QB, Georgia : The next three weekends will have a massive impact on Stockton's candidacy. After the upcoming annual neutral-site matchup with rival Florida, Georgia—which was idle last Saturday—plays at Ole Miss and hosts Missouri. All three SEC foes are currently ranked.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State : Mestemaker torched Colorado for 386 yards and four touchdowns in a 57-24 rout. He's second nationally with 2,326 passing yards, leading OSU to a 5-2 record with a trip to Iowa State looming.

Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss : In a 34-27 loss at Texas, Chambliss had a career-worst three interceptions. The performance dinged his résumé as the Rebels dipped to 5-2. Still, he's Ole Miss's most important player. The Rebels have reputation-restoring chances at home against Auburn and Georgia in the next two weeks.

Braden Atkinson, QB, Oregon State : Look, if everyone else is falling due to losses, someone has to rise, no? Atkinson has quietly excelled for a rising program, posting FBS-best marks of 2,604 passing yards and 24 touchdowns. This weekend's trip to Fresno State is huge for Oregon State's team upside—and, in turn, how high Atkinson may climb in award discussions.

Gio Lopez, QB, Wake Forest : Rested after an idle weekend, Lopez and the Demon Deacons host Virginia this Saturday. He's racked up 2,200 offensive yards and 23 touchdowns while propelling Wake to a 6-1 record.

Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs 📝

Last time out, CJ Carr and the Fighting Irish fell in a dramatic finish at BYU. The loss ended Notre Dame's 16-game unbeaten streak.

But the path to the College Football Playoff is still wide open.

Although an outstanding defense is ND's strength, Carr has provided a steady hand offensively. He's thrown for 1,639 yards and 16 touchdowns, with one interception, and added 82 yards and three scores on the ground.

Week 10's home showdown with top-ranked Miami is peeking over the horizon, but Notre Dame takes on Navy this Saturday.

In a true sign-of-the-times moment, Jesse Legree announced he will be staying at Oregon State for the 2027 season.

Nevertheless, the news was a welcome development for a program that had drifted in FBS purgatory after the Pac-12 crumbled. Legree, a typical 3-star talent who's turned into a national star as a freshman, will be the cornerstone of the Beavers' recruiting pitch moving forward.

Also, the season is barely half over. We're not handing out awards just yet.

Legree has reeled in 46 passes and stands atop the country with 1,040 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns. Those are incredible numbers, but a matchup at Fresno State kicks off a challenging final stretch for OSU.

Nobody is unstoppable. Malachi Toney seems awfully close to it, though.

Last weekend, he shattered a Miami single-game record with 16 receptions while gashing Pitt for 194 yards and three scores.

The sophomore wideout has corralled an FBS-high 66 catches. That has gone for 952 yards and 11 touchdowns—both of which are third in the country, trailing only Oregon State's Legree and Ohio State's Smith.

North Carolina isn't elite, but the defense has yielded a modest 6.3 yards per pass attempt. Toney won't necessarily dominate UNC in a night game on the road.

At the same time, should we expect anything less?

Given how strongly Darian Mensah leans on Toney, should they be flipped? There's a good argument in favor of that.

Mensah, however, has been similarly fantastic for 7-0 Miami.

Boasting an FBS-best 81.4 percent completion rate and 10.5 yards per attempt, he's thrown for 2,151 yards and 22 touchdowns with a lone interception. Mensah has also chipped in 73 yards and two scores as a runner.

If the 'Canes dispatch UNC on Saturday, they'll create a Heisman-worthy moment for Mensah (and Toney) at Notre Dame in Week 10.

Toney and Mensah are rising. That is inarguable.

Nonetheless, Jeremiah Smith has reinforced his billing as the best player in the country so far. He fully deserves the Heisman front-runner label.

Julian Sayin's injury is a double-edged sword for Smith, though.

If he continues to thrive with a backup QB, his reputation only improves. Smith is talented enough to elevate the offense. But there's a very real, very understandable possibility that Ohio State struggles behind an inexperienced signal-caller and Smith's production suffers.

One way or another, those hypotheticals will start to get tested in Week 9 as the Buckeyes travel to USC and then enter a tough November slate.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs after Week 8
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included are each player's numbers through the air and on the ground, their game's outcome, and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight the quality of the opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F. Those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 14-of-23, 149 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 34 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Washington State) Week 8 Outcome: Win (31-10)

The Boise State offense is built on the running game, as they rank seventh in the nation with 237.9 rushing yards per game and have the nation's leading rusher in Dylan Riley (140 carries, 963 yards, 8 TD).

That helps open up the passing game for third-year starter Maddux Madsen, but he deserves credit for his efficiency when he pushes the ball downfield. He has thrown 14 touchdown passes without an interception. His 65.6 percent completion rate is a significant improvement on last year's 58.3 percent mark.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 17-of-23, 305 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 2 carries, -8 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Navy) Week 8 Outcome: Win (49-39)

A former 4-star recruit who made stops at Tennessee, Indiana and UCF over his first four collegiate seasons, Tayven Jackson has found a home at North Texas this year as one of the AAC's top quarterbacks.

He recorded his third straight 300-yard passing game on Saturday to help North Texas improve to 5-2 on the year. He now leads the AAC in passing yards (2,173), yards per attempt (9.8) and passer rating (177.3).

Week 8 Passing Stats: 19-of-30, 172 yards, 4 TD, 2 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 12 carries, 46 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Texas Tech) Week 8 Outcome: Win (37-24)

After three seasons at Georgia Southern, including a 2,929-yard, 20-touchdown campaign last year, JC French IV landed at Cincinnati in the transfer portal as the replacement for Brendan Sorbsy.

Despite two interceptions on Saturday, his four touchdown passes helped drive the upset win over previously undefeated Texas Tech. He now has seven touchdown passes in the last two weeks after recording just six total over his first five games.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 29-of-43, 320 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 31 yards, 2 TD Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (East Carolina) Week 8 Outcome: Win (41-34, OT)

After throwing three interceptions in a loss to Tulane in Week 7, Marcus Stokes matched a season high with five total touchdowns on Saturday. His go-ahead rushing score in overtime held up as the game-winner.

He leads the AAC in total yards (2,392) and total touchdowns (23), ranking in the top 10 nationally in both categories. The West Florida transfer has looked the part this year after making the jump from D-II.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 19-of-26, 203 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 23 yards, 1 TD Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Vanderbilt) Week 8 Outcome: Win (34-17)

Kentucky clinched a winning record in SEC play for just the third time since 1977 with Saturday's victory over Vanderbilt. Notre Dame transfer Kenny Minchey has played a major role in their unexpected success.

Picked to finish 14th in the preseason media poll, the Wildcats are now up to No. 9 in the latest AP poll, behind only No. 3 Georgia among conference foes. With 1,755 passing yards and a 14-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio, Minchey has done an excellent job piloting the offense for one of the nation's biggest surprises.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 19-of-25, 219 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 12 carries, 83 yards, 2 TD Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Rutgers) Week 8 Outcome: Win (42-14)

Two years after completing fewer than 60 percent of his passes and leading the Big Ten with 11 interceptions as the starter at Michigan State, Aidan Chiles has helped transform Northwestern into a dark-horse playoff contender.

The meaty part of the schedule is still on the horizon with Oregon, Iowa and Ohio State the next three weeks, but he leads the Big Ten with a 71.3 percent completion rate and has steered the Wildcats to a 6-1 start and the No. 24 spot in the latest AP poll.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 7-of-15, 79 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 20 carries, 87 yards, 2 TD Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (TCU) Week 8 Outcome: Win (24-20)

Michael Hawkins Jr. was more of a running back lining up under center than anything resembling a traditional quarterback on Saturday. He now ranks 11th in the nation with 836 rushing yards and is tied for the FBS lead with 16 rushing touchdowns.

Zooming out on his dual-threat abilities, he also has 1,598 passing yards, 11 passing touchdowns and a Big 12-leading 10.1 yards per attempt. After three straight losses to start conference play, the Mountaineers have won back-to-back games and are now one victory away from bowl eligibility after finishing 4-8 a year ago.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 32-of-45, 387 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 54 yards, 1 TD Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Auburn) Week 8 Outcome: Win (38-17)

Sam Leavitt threw at least one interception in each of LSU's first six games, but he has put together back-to-back standout performances against Mississippi State and Auburn with seven touchdowns, zero interceptions and a terrific 75.9 percent completion rate.

Looking beyond his early turnover struggles, he leads the SEC in completions (180), passing yards (2,163), passing touchdowns (17) and total touchdowns (25). The Tigers are all the way up to No. 15 in the latest AP poll after tumbling to No. 22 a few weeks ago.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 16-of-32, 257 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 15 carries, 37 yards, 1 TD Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (UCF) Week 8 Outcome: Loss (31-39, 2OT)

Bear Bachmeier had multiple chances to help BYU avoid Saturday's shocking upset to UCF, but the Cougars' offense went three-and-out on back-to-back possessions at the end of regulation. He threw three straight incompletions to end the second overtime and the game.

With a 50 percent completion rate and 2.5 yards per carry, his dual-threat talents were effectively contained. BYU will get a chance to regroup next weekend at home against a middling Arizona State squad.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 20-of-32, 156 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 16 carries, 14 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Clemson) Week 8 Outcome: Win (20-16)

Ethan Grunkemeyer was held below 200 passing yards for the second time this season, but he played mistake-free football and led an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning touchdown with 1:44 remaining.

The Hokies have leaned heavily on the Penn State transfer offensively. He leads the ACC in completions (187) while ranking second in attempts (261). The redshirt sophomore has three years of eligibility left and the potential to become a top-tier quarterback.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 18-of-26, 204 yards, 0 TD, 2 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 15 carries, 150 yards, 2 TD Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Houston) Week 8 Outcome: Win (21-13)

Despite throwing a pair of interceptions, Devon Dampier made a massive impact with his legs and scored the go-ahead rushing touchdown with 2:09 remaining to keep Utah undefeated.

It was the first game all season in which he didn't throw multiple touchdown passes. His 68.7 percent completion rate is an improvement on last year's 63.5 percent mark, but he has already surpassed the five interceptions he threw a year ago.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 21-of-36, 386 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 8 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Colorado) Week 8 Outcome: Win (57-24)

Over his last five games, Drew Mestemaker has completed nearly 70 percent of his passes for 1,768 yards with 17 touchdowns and two interceptions, looking more and more like the same quarterback who led the nation in passing yards (4,379) a year ago at North Texas.

This weekend's performance came against a Colorado defense that allowed more than 30 points per game, but a 386-yard, four-touchdown performance against anyone is a solid day's work.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 19-of-30, 311 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, 20 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Texas A&M) Week 8 Outcome: Win (31-20)

After turning the ball over three times in a disappointing road loss to Tennessee in Week 7, Keelon Russell bounced back nicely with his third 300-yard, three-touchdown passing performance of the season.

His 2,308 total yards trail only LSU's Sam Leavitt (2,487) on the SEC leaderboard. He has 20 total touchdowns through eight games. Those two dual-threat standouts will go head-to-head on Nov. 7 in a clash of two-loss playoff contenders that will likely be an elimination game for the loser.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 27-of-34, 308 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 18 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Iowa State) Week 8 Outcome: Win (39-3)

Arizona put points on the board in each of its first four offensive possessions to build a 25-3 halftime lead, then cruised to victory to improve to 6-1 overall and 3-1 in Big 12 conference play.

Noah Fifita kicked off the scoring with a 71-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Mizell on the second play of the game. After another efficient passing performance, he now ranks second in the nation with a 74.2 percent completion rate.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 16-of-23, 223 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 26 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (California) Week 8 Outcome: Win (59-20)

Kevin Jennings has now gone three straight games without an interception after some early turnover issues. He became SMU's all-time leader with his 73rd career passing touchdown in Saturday's victory.

The three-year starter now holds the top spot in completions (781), passing yards (9,771) and passing touchdowns (74). While several contenders have suffered their second loss in recent weeks, he quietly has a 6-1 SMU squad up to No. 19 in the latest AP poll.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 8-of-18, 81 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 7 yards, 1 TD Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Michigan) Week 8 Outcome: Win (13-6, OT)

The Michigan secondary has surrendered 154.6 passing yards per game this year. That is the seventh-lowest total among FBS teams and the third-lowest among major conference defenses. In other words, Josh Hoover is not the first quarterback to struggle to move the ball against the Wolverines.

That said, he didn't have a single completion after halftime until Indiana's possession in overtime. He ultimately scored the game-winning touchdown on a quarterback keeper, but it was an ugly day under center. Hoover still appeared banged up from the Week 7 loss to Ohio State.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 25-of-52, 250 yards, 2 TD, 3 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 7 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Texas) Week 8 Outcome: Loss (27-34)

Trinidad Chambliss had never thrown multiple interceptions in a game during his time at Ole Miss prior to Saturday's three-interception performance against Texas, matching his total for the entirety of the 2025 season.

Zooming out, the more troubling trend might be his 51.1 percent completion rate over the last two weeks. He managed to make things interesting with a pair of second-half touchdown passes after the Rebels trailed 24-3 at halftime, but he was unable to orchestrate a game-tying drive after they recovered an onside kick in the final two minutes.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 31-of-50, 258 yards, 1 TD, 2 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, -57 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Wisconsin) Week 8 Outcome: Loss (7-24)

The USC offense ran into a brick wall against Wisconsin's defense, finishing with the fewest points ever scored by a Lincoln Riley-coached team en route to the Trojans' second loss of the season.

Jayden Maiava is still the Big Ten leader in completions (183), passing yards (2,302) and passing touchdowns (19), but he had his worst game of the season on Saturday. Even without the 57 yards lost on five Wisconsin sacks, the USC running game still produced just 40 yards on 20 carries. He was unable to shoulder the load in the passing game.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 19-of-35, 282 yards, 0 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 20 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Utah) Week 8 Outcome: Loss (13-21)

Conner Weigman had a crucial fumble after being crushed by blitzing safety Jackson Bennee late in the fourth quarter. The Utes iced the victory with a Devon Dampier rushing touchdown on the next play.

Prior to that, it had still been a relatively quiet game for Houston's quarterback. He failed to record a touchdown after entering play with 26 total touchdowns through seven games.

Week 8 Passing Stats: 31-of-37, 387 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 8 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, -12 yards Week 8 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Pitt) Week 8 Outcome: Win (52-23)

The gap between Darian Mensah and the rest of the nation's quarterbacks continues to grow, as he lit up the Pitt defense for his fourth 300-yard passing game and his second with at least four passing touchdowns.

More than half of his 31 completions went to Malachi Toney, who finished with 16 catches for 194 yards and three touchdowns. Mensah is the FBS leader in completion percentage (81.4), yards per attempt (10.5) and passer rating (204.6). He is Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith's biggest competition in the Heisman race.

To keep things fresh and include breakout performers, we will re-rank the top 20 quarterbacks each week on this final slide. That will then reset the field for next week's report cards.

Quarterbacks with a Week 9 bye who are performing at a top-20 level were still included in the updated rankings to show how they stack up to the field.

articles.title: Xabi ya se lo había imaginado
articles.standfirst: 'Se puede pitar', por Delfín Melero
articles.summary: 'Se puede pitar', por Delfín Melero
articles.body: Ni el Real Madrid estaba muerto ni José Mourinho había vuelto al Bernabéu para jubilarse. Iban al matadero, y no es que salieran vivos del Camp Nou, es que los jugadores salieron señalándose el escudo y el técnico, dejando la huella de sus rodillas en el verde, cosa seria. Otra celebración icónica, el Mou de siempre, el Madrid de siempre. Un equipo en el amplio sentido de la palabra, que es mucho decir viniendo de donde se viene. El Clásico demostró que se podía, claro que se podía. Xabi Alonso no estaba tan loco. En Londres, el de tolosarra lo vería y vería reflejado lo que un día imaginó. Se podía jugar así. Es el equipo comprometido que buscaba y que ha conseguido Mourinho porque le han dejado. Con Valverde de lateral, por su bien y el de sus compañeros. Con Tchouaméni y al lado un fichaje con brillo en la botas, un tal Bernardo Silva, que merece un respeto. Es un tipo al que no le tiemblan las piernas con el balón, uno que sabe mantener la tranquilidad incluso en una bañera con pirañas, un 'Xabi' de la vida. El nuevo Madrid es un equipo con Arda Güler al mando, con el pelo para atrás y la mirada hacia delante. Balones para el turco, el mejor lanzador de los atletas. Un Real con Diomande, que no estaba el año pasado y estuvo en el Camp Nou... también porque no estaba Vinicius. Lamine tembló con Cucurella cada vez que le vio el pelo también por las ayudas del marfileño. Xabi se lo había imaginado como Mourinho, pero él sí pudo hacerlo. Aunque puedas, también hay que atreverse, claro. Dejarse barba invita a ser más valiente. En el Clásico se jugó a lo que quiso el Madrid. A lo que quiso Mourinho. A lo que habría querido Xabi, que lo había visto antes que nadie. Ahora hay un plan y vía libre para acometerlo. Más vale tarde que nunca. Hasta Vinicius puede subirse al tren si quiere... con el peligro de que ya está en movimiento.
