articles.title: Lyft driver ejects four women after Portland Thorns protest, then one finds her account deactivated
articles.summary: Julie Lane says a Lyft driver kicked her group out in a dark Portland area after spotting their "Save Women's Sports" shirts from the Thorns game.
articles.body: Julie Lane had already been struck by a Portland Thorns fan, sending her tumbling over two rows of seats. The Bay Area resident was one of about 20 people at Friday's National Women's Soccer League game wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts and holding a "Save Women's Sports" sign. The demonstration drew verbal and physical backlash from other spectators, prompting Providence Park security to remove Lane and the rest of the group. So you could understand why, after all that, Lane would just want to get back to her hotel. Unfortunately for her and three other women, a Lyft driver made this much harder than it needed to be. After picking up the quartet from the stadium, the driver asked the group, "are you the ladies from the news?" Thinking he was on their side, Linda Serbu answered with an enthusiastic yes. BRANDI KRUSE TELLS LAURA INGRAHAM ABOUT BEING FORCED OUT OF PORTLAND SOCCER GAME: 'WE DID NOTHING WRONG' That, according to Lane, is when the driver pulled over and told them to get out. He said "it's my own private car, and I can cancel any ride I want to, and you don't belong in my car," Lane said. Keep in mind that most of these women were over 50. Serbu had a walker that the driver loaded up in the trunk. But none of them had any idea where they were when he told them to get out. And Lane? Lane refused to leave the vehicle. There were two reasons for her resistance. The first is that she paid for a ride and didn't feel as though she had done anything wrong. This, essentially, was a driver ejecting them for their political views and fashion choices. The second is that she felt genuinely unsafe. These women weren't being chucked next to a shopping mall in broad daylight. According to Lane, it was "a dark corner of Portland." Nevertheless, the driver called the police with the intention of having the ladies arrested for trespassing if they were still in his car. He admitted as much in a Reddit post, where he described the women as "anti-trans agitators." Lane welcomed the police call, saying "please go ahead and get the cops here. I'd love to talk to them about this." But they were gone before any of Portland's finest showed up. Another woman ordered an Uber, which arrived a few minutes later and took the group to its destination. This happened as Lane was on the phone with a Lyft support representative, who said the driver was going to be disciplined. But much to Lane's surprise the next morning — as she was awaiting a scheduled Lyft ride — she discovered that Lyft had deactivated her account. Asked for comment on the whole ordeal, a Lyft spokesperson wrote the following in an email to OutKick. 'SAVE WOMEN’S SPORTS' ACTIVISTS EJECTED FROM NWSL MATCH AFTER BEING STRUCK, CONFRONTED BY PRO-TRANS CROWD CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Everyone deserves to feel safe and respected on the Lyft platform, and discrimination of any kind has no place in our community. Our Safety team was in contact with both the rider and the driver involved and we are continuing to review the incident." The driver's actions may also have violated Portland city regulations. Under Section 16.40.280(C)(13) of the city code, rideshare drivers are prohibited from refusing to transport passengers of "proper demeanor" to destinations within Portland after accepting their rides. But he doesn't seem to feel an ounce of remorse, with his Reddit post reading like a 380-word back pat. He lamented that it took security more than 15 minutes to eject the XX-XY crowd from the stadium, and wrote "Please address this by making better efforts to keep fans safe at Providence Park, especially those in the LGBTQ + community." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Serbu found that line ironic. "He admits that he kicked us out for our T-shirts and our, quote, 'anti-LGB activism,' or something. And just to clarify, we were two lesbians and two bisexual women," she said. Probably a safe bet that none of these women will be moving to Portland any time soon. Even after leaving the stadium, they were met with incessant boos and middle fingers from Thorns fans. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A Lyft driver bouncing them from his car for expressing a viewpoint the vast majority of Americans agree with was the final indignity.

articles.title: Celtic: One year on from Martin O'Neill's return to Scottish champions after Brendan Rodgers' shock departure
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill returned on an interim basis following Brendan Rodgers' decision to resign; he left following Wilfried Nancy's appointment, before returning after his sacking; the 74-year-old agreed to become permanent boss after leading Celtic to a league and cup double last season
articles.body:
Just a few months after a double-winning season, making it four titles in a row and taking Bayern Munich all the way in the Champions League knockouts, the club ended up in crisis.

Manager Brendan Rodgers walked out on the club after a row with principal shareholder Dermot Desmond, sending shockwaves across world football.

Club legend Martin O'Neill, who had been a pundit for the last six years and is now 74 years old, took the reins temporarily in yet another surprise development to this incredible story.

But how did Celtic get into such a situation, and what happened next?

It was at 9.44pm on Monday, October 27, 2025, that Celtic released a statement on their website entitled, 'Brendan Rodgers leaves Celtic Football Club'.

It was just five paragraphs long, announcing that Rodgers had handed in his resignation and the club had accepted it. It also revealed that former boss O'Neill was taking over on an interim basis with Shaun Maloney, while they began the process to appoint a permanent manager.

This shock news came on the back of Celtic's 3-1 defeat to Hearts at Tynecastle the day before, which meant they trailed the Edinburgh club by eight points in the title race.

Rodgers had become increasingly frustrated with the board and had been very vocal about it.

The Irishman had hoped the club would build on the success of the previous season which saw them go toe-to-toe with Europe's elite in the Champions League - making it out of the league phase and then very nearly knocking Bayern Munich out in the play-offs.

This time, Celtic had a qualifying play-off against Kairat Almaty to negotiate to reach the Champions League.

The club had made £75m from the previous season's Champions League exploits. There was plenty of cash and Rodgers was expecting investment. The fans demanded investment.

But Celtic went into the tie with Kairat still without replacements for Kyogo Furuhashi, who was sold to Rennes in January 2025 for £10m, and Nicolas Kuhn, who left for Como that summer for £16.5m.

They were beaten by the Kazakh side on penalties. They then also sold Adam Idah, leaving them with just one first team striker - Daizen Maeda - at the club after the summer transfer window.

This sparked mass protests against the board at games and Rodgers appeared to feel vindicated to speak out also about his frustrations with the lack of reinforcements in key areas, where players had departed.

After a defeat to Dundee at Dens Park, he said: "There's no way you'll go into a race and be given the keys to a Honda Civic and say, 'I want you to drive it like a Ferrari'. It's not going to happen."

Celtic's principal shareholder Desmond wanted to meet the manager the day after the defeat to Hearts.

It's understood it was a three-hour meeting in which a major row led to an ultimatum being given by Desmond: get on with the job, or resign - he wasn't going to be sacked.

Rodgers, who had previously promised the fans that this time he would at least see out his contract at Celtic, chose to walk away from the job.

When news filtered through to other board members and club staff, there was absolute shock. Nobody expected things to escalate in the way they did.

The announcement made national and international headlines. What added fuel to the fire was another statement on the Celtic website, written by Desmond, who came out all guns blazing with a character assassination of Celtic's third-most successful manager.

Desmond labelled Rodgers "divisive, misleading, and self-serving," stating that his recent conduct broke the trust placed in him upon his return to the club. The Irish billionaire disputed Rodgers' public complaints about transfer backing, stating that every player signed and sold during his tenure had Rodgers' full knowledge, approval, and endorsement.

He claimed that during the meeting with Rodgers, the Celtic boss could not identify a single instance of the club obstructing or failing to support him.

Desmond said that Rodgers' public narrative created a toxic environment and triggered unwarranted abuse toward board members and executives.

Rodgers, who now manages Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah, has still not publicly responded to the claims, nor has he talked about his Celtic exit to this day.

It was a bombshell statement from Desmond on a night that rocked Celtic to the core.

Many Celtic fans were in shock as they woke up to the news that Rodgers had left. But it was just as a big shock to find out that O'Neill was the man back in charge of the club.

The then 73-year-old hadn't been a football manager since 2019 when he left Nottingham Forest, and even he revealed his surprise at being asked by Desmond to lead the club.

But he accepted the job and got on with the task, while the club began the process to appoint a permanent manager.

He stressed that he was just back until the club found a new, "younger" manager.

He got a hero's welcome in his first game two days after being appointed - a 4-0 win over Falkirk at Celtic Park. He joked that he didn't know some of the players' names.

Next up, O'Neill had the small matter of a derby match with Rangers in the League Cup semi-final at Hampden Park. In true O'Neill fashion, he won that 3-1 after extra time to send Celtic into a final against St Mirren at the end of December.

The only blip in his initial return was a 3-1 away defeat to Midtjylland in the Europa League, but he more than made up for it with an historic night in Rotterdam as Celtic beat Feyenoord 3-1 last November.

That Europa League win put them in a good position to qualify for the knockouts, while Celtic also notched victories over Kilmarnock, St Mirren, Hibernian and Dundee in the league.

Seven wins out of eight games - O'Neill had more than just steadied the ship by December for the new, incoming boss Wilfried Nancy. He'd taken a fairly flat Celtic team and put them back level on points with Hearts, into a cup final and gave them a huge away win in Europe.

In his 'farewell speech' at Celtic Park on December 3, 2025, O'Neill said: "They (the players) have been absolutely fantastic. It's been a real privilege. I've had the time of my life in the past five to six weeks."

The Hoops boss then sailed off into the sunset and back to London in time for Christmas.

Nancy couldn't get going as Celtic manager - losing six of his eight games in charge, including the cup final to St Mirren, a top-of-the-table clash against Hearts and at home to Rangers in the New Year Derby.

After only 33 days he was sacked, becoming Celtic's shortest-serving manager.

O'Neill was back exactly a month later. And he had one job: deliver the title.

He did that in the most dramatic fashion against title rivals Hearts on the last day of the season, with three minutes to spare. It was one of the most turbulent and chaotic seasons in Celtic's recent history, but O'Neill made sure it was still a successful one by winning the double.

After taking a break at the end of the season, O'Neill agreed to become the club's permanent manager in June by signing a one-year deal with the option to extend by a further year.

Celtic are still going through the motions on and off the field, but one man they can be grateful for is Martin O'Neill for twice stepping forward in their hour of need and saving their season.

articles.title: El Castellón es líder con la mejor defensa de las tres principales categorías
articles.standfirst: Los albinegros han encajado 4 goles en 11 partidos
articles.summary: Los albinegros han encajado cuatro goles en once partidos
articles.body: El Castellón ha retomado el liderato de Segunda división dejando de nuevo la portería a cero en la goleada firmada frente al Sporting (4-0). Se trata del séptimo partido de la temporada en el que los albinegros no reciben gol, lo que confirma la fortaleza de un equipo cuya mentalidad es claramente ofensiva. Los orelluts han recibido sólo 4 tantos en 11 jornadas, lo que les sitúa como el equipo menos goleado de las tres principales categorías del fútbol español. Y eso con una jornada más que en Primera y dos más que en Primera RFEF. El conjunto que más se les acerca es el Cacereño, del Grupo I de Primera RFEF, que ha recibido 5. En Segunda, el equipo que más rivaliza con el Castellón en el apartado defensivo es el Mallorca, que ha encajado 6. Mejor defensa con propuesta de ataque El mérito del Castellón es doble, pues este registro lo ha logrado con un estilo enfocado claramente en el ataque. Los albinegros vienen jugando con una defensa de tres, con Mellot, Alberto y Sienra como integrantes habituales, y un portero, Matthys, que está siendo fundamental con sus intervenciones. Los orelluts acumulan mucha gente arriba y, de hecho, son el equipo que más goles ha marcado en Segunda hasta el momento, pero una de sus grandes cualidades es su repliegue organizado para minimizar las situaciones de transición. El entrenador del Castellón espera que esta dinámica tenga continuidad. "Recibir sólo 4 goles en 11 partidos es muy difícil en esta competición y nos tiene que servir para verlo como un reto de seguir en la misma línea de cara a mantenernos en la parte alta y conseguir el objetivo", ha declarado Pablo Hernández.

articles.title: Are Chelsea finally playing the brand of football Sonia Bompastor wants - and is it WSL title-worthy?
articles.summary: Digital journalist Laura Hunter returns for a second season with a WSL-dedicated column, analysing all the big talking points from across the weekend's action; this week's focus is on Chelsea's resurgence and Man Utd's swift development under Eva Olid
articles.body:
It's been a long time since Chelsea entered a domestic campaign as underdogs. The bookies might have had them as favourites to win the WSL title before a ball was kicked but most hardened observers chose Man City as the more likely champions. The market appeared to be hedging their bets on history.

While I still believe Man City are the team to beat, Chelsea's start to the season cannot be ignored. After seven played they are top by virtue of goal difference, with a perfect record since their opening day draw with Aston Villa. City and Chelsea's results in a head-to-head count are actually identical - but of course the nip and tuck is more nuanced than that.

Chelsea's win from behind to beat Crystal Palace at the weekend, without Keira Walsh or Lauren James, was a deliberate show of strength. And an indication of Sonia Bompastor's intent to balance her squad between priorities. The Blues host Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Are they equipped to sustain such momentum? The numbers suggest they are well placed to compete with Man City. Chelsea are the league's top scorers, best chance creators and have conceded the fewest goals against. Dig a bit deeper into the data and their improved output presents the picture of a team revitalised.

It may have taken two years, but Bompastor has finally got her wish. The Frenchwoman always wanted her side to have greater technical control but was struggling to get the arrangement right, especially in midfield. At long last, Chelsea are a team with an identifiable attacking style, based on the principles of progressive, possession-orientated football.

The system relies heavily on high-advancing full-backs, who are dynamic enough to stretch the pitch in possession and make it more compact when the ball is lost. Ellie Carpenter and Katie McCabe are perfect for the role.

Carpenter is the WSL's best in class when it comes to two-way influence. She ranks as the league's highest-performing defender in terms of goals scored (3), shots taken (17), touches in the opposition box (49) and open-play crosses (40). She and McCabe have generated 17 chances for team-mates apiece.

In central areas, the introduction of Lexi Potter has encouraged a higher role for Keira Walsh and the combination has meant Chelsea are able to dictate tempo with greater success and variation. Aesthetically, Chelsea are a better watch, but crucially, with more reliable end product.

Melvine Malard was an inspired signing in the summer, boasting four WSL goals from four starts so far, matched by the consistency of James. Goals are coming from elsewhere, too, as the intensity of Chelsea's midfield press continues to generate high turnovers and therefore opportunities for lesser-known scorers. Walsh and Sjoeke Nusken have bagged four between them.

Such consistency of delivery is enough to excite even the most skeptical of spectators. And Bompastor must take credit too, making two changes at half-time against Palace to turn the result on its head.

No doubt Chelsea in a relentless rhythm spells danger for the competition. Only time will tell if such an uptick means they remain close chasers of Man City - or have in fact managed to overtake them.

Are Man Utd in better shape than first thought?

Man City won 3-0 home and away in the derby last season. It was the least competitive that fixture had been for some time. And there was plenty to suggest a similar pattern would repeat itself this term, given City's perfect start and United's patchy evolution under Eva Olid.

But Olid's side have turned a corner in recent weeks. Now on a four-game unbeaten streak, the Spaniard's possession-led approach is starting to take recognisable shape.

Against Charlton last Sunday, United completed 700 passes with an accuracy of 88.7 per cent. Both club record high figures in a WSL game. This week, they went toe-to-toe with the league's pass-masters and boasted an equal share of the ball, landing more accurate passes overall and a higher amount in the opposition half. Few sides are technically capable of doing that to City.

"If you want to see the progression of this United team, this is a great example of it," said Sky Sports' Izzy Christiansen on co-comms at Leigh Sports Village. United were breaking lines with the frequency of a side who had been modelled on this tactical plan for years.

Jess Park in particular was outstanding, involved prolifically in the build-up phase. She is the glue. The ball-carrier, but also the player with the cognitive ability to play in a way that accepts responsibility for being at the heart of every attack. Importance is placed on Ella Toone too.

Such numbers represent more than baby steps. It's evidence that United's squad, fairly modest in size, can produce the systematic style Olid prefers while also getting results. To be the first to take points off City is a triumph in itself. They have jumped into fourth in the table as reward.

Of course there are many more layers to this approach and Olid is relying on key contributors to make it work consistently. But major ground has been broken over the past six weeks. The manager is clearly enthused: "How this team has built in confidence from day one to now, in a short period of time, the progression has been massive."

articles.title: Mbappé pide disculpas: "Siento un profundo respeto por el pueblo chino y su historia y estoy sinceramente arrepentido"
articles.standfirst: El francés emite un comunicado en tres idiomas y sale al paso para zanjar la polémica provocada por sus palabras
articles.summary: El francés emite un comunicado en tres idiomas y sale al paso para zanjar la polémica provocada por sus palabras
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé ha tenido que salir al paso de la polémica generada por sus declaraciones recientes sobre China que han provocado un malestar en el país asiático, hasta el punto de que se habían cancelado las retransmisiones de los partidos del Real Madrid. El delantero ha emitido un comunicado oficial en tres idiomas (chino, francés e inglés) en el que pide disculpas por unas palabras que han herido la sensibilidad de la comunidad china. "Durante una entrevista reciente, reaccioné a una imagen mía en la que aparecía representado. Mi comentario fue desafortunado y ahora comprendo que ha herido a muchas personas en China y entre la comunidad china de todo el mundo", explica el futbolista francés en un comunicado firmado este martes 27 de octubre en París. Mbappé reconoce así su error y admite el malestar provocado por sus palabras, aunque no entra en más detalles. El delantero madridista cierra su comunicado con una disculpa y un mensaje de respeto hacia el país asiático: "Pido disculpas a todas las personas a las que mis palabras hayan ofendido. No era en absoluto mi intención. Siento un profundo respeto por el pueblo chino y su historia, y estoy sinceramente arrepentido". Con este mensaje, Mbappé trata de zanjar una polémica que había obligado intervenir hasta LaLiga, que había censurado las palabras de la estrella del Real Madrid, que había dicho que le hacían gracia "los memes" tras su campaña de publicidad en China. "Con el que más me he reído es ése en el que usan mi cara en un dictador chino. Lo utilizo mucho con mis amigos", dijo el francés, que ya se ha disculpado.

articles.title: The Ballon d’Or has a narrow definition of footballing greatness
articles.summary: Celebrity, bias towards players in attack and European dominance undermine football’s most prestigious individual award.
articles.body:
The Ballon d’Or is football’s most prestigious individual honour. On Monday, Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane became the first Englishman to win it since Michael Owen in 2001. But his victory also raises a fundamental question about the award: How can individual excellence be fairly assessed in a team sport?

For much of the past two decades, that question has been overshadowed by the extraordinary rivalry between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. From 2008 to 2017, one or the other won the Ballon d’Or every year, turning the annual award into a contest between the two superstars. Messi eventually accumulated a record eight trophies and Ronaldo five, together accounting for 13 of the 17 awards presented between 2008 and 2025.

Their rivalry generated unprecedented excitement around an award first presented in 1956, when England’s “wizard of the dribble”, Sir Stanley Matthews, became its inaugural winner. But it also pushed several important questions into the background. Has the growing commercialisation of the Ballon d’Or distracted from its purpose? Why does it overwhelmingly reward attacking players? And why does a supposedly global award remain so heavily focused on European football?

The commercialisation of the Ballon d’Or reflects the transformation of football into a global entertainment industry, in which individual players have become brands in their own right.

“The whole dynamic of the Ballon d’Or has changed because the dynamic of the sports and entertainment industry has changed with the way individual athletes are marketed,” Steve Martin, founding partner of MSQ Sport + Entertainment, formerly of M&C Saatchi, told The Athletic.

“They’ve found a way as an individual athlete or player to build their own profile and their own fanbase, as opposed to relying on their clubs. They control their own destiny, and they market themselves.”

Former Switzerland defender Ramon Vega has been more critical of this development. “The commercialisation and monetisation of this award is not taking it in the right direction,” he told the writer.

The Ballon d’Or has undoubtedly become a bigger spectacle, but the attention surrounding the award should not obscure the question of what constitutes individual excellence. And commercialisation is not its only problem. The award has also long favoured players in attack over those in other positions.

A goalkeeper’s or defender’s performance is as important as that of midfielders and strikers, in a sport where a team is supposed to be as great as the sum of its parts. Yet Russia’s Lev Yashin remains the only goalkeeper to have won the award, in 1963, while Italy’s Fabio Cannavaro was the last defender to do so, in 2006, after captaining his country to World Cup victory. Germany’s Franz Beckenbauer and Matthias Sammer were among the few other defenders to have received the honour.

“Goalkeepers and defenders are also part of the spectacle. Attackers don’t just play amongst themselves,” Cannavaro told France Football after winning the award in 2006. “If a goalkeeper has saved 15 or so matches in a year, it’s only fair to highlight him.”

But the Italian’s observations have done little to change the pervasive bias of voters for the award, as strikers and midfielders on the European club and national team stage remain the yardstick for measuring global excellence.

That focus on European football points to another longstanding weakness of the Ballon d’Or: Its failure to adequately recognise outstanding players from elsewhere in the world.

For nearly four decades after the award was established, only European players were eligible to win it. This was a great injustice to exceptional footballers from other continents, even those competing in Europe’s leading leagues. The late Diego Maradona was perhaps the most notable victim of this exclusion.

The restriction was finally lifted in 1995, allowing players of any nationality at European clubs to compete for the prize. It took another 12 years, until 2007, for the award to be opened to players competing anywhere in the world.

It could be argued that when the award began, the club and national team game outside Europe was beyond the close observation and expert knowledge of the Ballon d’Or selectors. But that argument no longer holds water. Knowledge of the global game has grown exponentially, yet recognition of excellence beyond Europe’s leading competitions remains limited.

When Liberia’s George Weah became the first non-European player to win the Ballon d’Or in 1995, following outstanding performances for Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan, his victory was expected to open the door for exceptional players from parts of the footballing world that had long been denied recognition.

But 31 years on, the former president of Liberia remains the only person outside Europe and South America to have won it.

“When I started playing football, I never thought I would ever win the Ballon d’Or and emerge as the best player in the world. I just had a passion for the game and I worked hard. Every day. I would rather train than eat or sleep,” Weah told the writer in Monrovia.

“I am surprised that no other African player has won the award since I did so. I think there have been others that deserve to win. But it is down to those who select the winners.”

Cameroon’s Samuel Eto’o, the former Barcelona and Inter striker, now president of his country’s football federation, is one person with a right to feel aggrieved that he didn’t win the award before retiring in 2019.

“It’s difficult to understand how Samuel Eto’o never won the Ballon d’Or with the impressive career he had,” Jose Mourinho, who managed Eto’o at Inter, said in a 2019 interview with Cameroon Radio.

“He played in three Champions League finals, winning two with Barcelona and scoring in both finals. He also won one Champions League at Inter and won many league titles. He was the best striker in the world for several years, and I think he deserved a Ballon d’Or, but these are things out of our control.”

Eto’o’s omission, like Weah’s continued status as the only African winner, raises questions about how the award’s selectors and voters assess the achievements of players from outside football’s traditional European and South American powerhouses.

The Ballon d’Or already has an international voting panel, with journalists from 100 countries selecting the winner from a shortlist of 30 players. But geographical representation among voters does not necessarily translate into recognition of the world’s footballing talent.

France Football, the award’s organisers, should ensure that the process of selecting nominees and winners draws on a genuinely global understanding of the game and gives due recognition to exceptional players, regardless of nationality or where they compete.

The award must also address its other shortcomings. Football is a team sport in which goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders and strikers all contribute to success, and individual recognition should reflect that. Nor should the growing commercial appeal of the Ballon d’Or distract from the footballing achievements it was created to honour.

The Ballon d’Or should be a celebration of individual excellence across all positions and all continents, not an award dominated by football’s biggest stars and Europe’s leading competitions. Only then can it truly claim to recognise the best footballer in the world.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: Castro: "Llegué con un segunda división en Francia hasta semifinales de Copa, vamos hacer lo mejor posible"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués del Levante afirma que dará descanso a los jugadores más habituales, aunque competirá para llegar lo más lejos posible
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués del Levante afirma que dará descanso a los jugadores más habituales, aunque competirá para llegar lo más lejos posible
articles.body: Sin rodeos. Luís Castro intentará hacer lo mejor posible a pesar de ser la Copa del Rey. El entrenador portugués del Levante ha querido sacar pecho de su pasado en el Dunkerque, equipo de segunda división en Francia, con el que llegó hasta semifinales, siendo eliminado por el PSG. A pesar de no quitarle importante, en detrimento de la liga, el luso ha admitted que " es una oportunidad para dar opciones a jugadores que lo merecen" e incluso, habrá presencia del filial en la convocatoria. Debut de Castro en la Copa del Rey "Es una competición que competimos para hacer lo mejor posible. Mi año en Francia, con el equipo en Segunda División, fuimos a semifinales de copa. Con esto puedes comprender como me tomo la competición. Eliminamos a tres equipos de primera división y fuimos eliminados por el PSG. Para llegar hasta donde llegamos, es porque la miro con muchas ganas de hacerlo mejor posible, como todos los partidos. Pero también es una oportunidad para dar opciones a jugadores que lo merecen" Enfermería "Dela y Enzo, continúan fuera. Brugué puede jugar normal. Está bien. Tenía una pequeña molestia y no preferimos no correr riesgos. Los cuatro últimos partidos estuvieron muy cerca, pero está bien. Está mejor de lo que estaba en el último partido" Jugadores sanos fuera de la convocatoria "Hay algún que otro jugador que se quedará fuera de la convocatoria. Si hubiera más tiempo entre partidos, podríamos pensar diferente, pero tenemos tan solo dos días. Como lo hacemos en liga, si no está al 100%, no arriesgamos" Marc Santos y Axel Tapé, posiciones "Son dos jugadores que pueden jugar en más de una posición. Tal vez, en ocasiones pueden jugar en posiciones donde necesitas pero Marc, por ejemplo, ha jugado en varias competiciones en tres posicione distintas y lo ha hecho muy bien. Axel también puede jugar porque lo ha hecho. Son dos jugadores que tienen esa calidad. Para mí es difícil decir en que posición juega mejor Marc, porque en los entrenamientos lo hace siempre bien. Tape estamos intentando hacerlo más fuerte en mediocampo pero es un jugador que puede jugar de central o de lateral" Oportunidad para la unidad B "Vamos a jugar con muchos jugadores que han sido titulares en varios partidos de la liga. a partir de ahí, no hay plan B ni plan A. Hay oportunidades que algunos tienen y tienen que demostrarlas. Si Ify hubiera debutado en Copa, vosotros diríais que "juega porque es la Copa y es el plan B", y no es así. Debutó en el campeonato porque era momento de ponerlo. Mañana habrá más cambios porque tiene otro partidos en dos días. Si pones a los mismos jugadores y vuelves a tener un partido dentro de dos días, seguro que alguno se lesiona. Yo no miro un plan b, si no una oportunidad para algunos. Es posible que ahora en copa jueguen su primer partido y luego en copa jueguen más partido" Aire fresco para jugadores cansados "La plantilla tiene algunos jugadores cansados, como es natural. Con este calendario y los horarios, es normal que estén cansados y que tengan más molestias" Tarancón, Rival "Al rival lo miramos como siempre. Lo miramos con mucha atención y tiene cosas muy interesantes. Yo he tenido una semifinales de copa, pero he ido a penaltis con un séptima división. Yo se lo que es la copa y se lo que puede pasar si no estás al 100%. Del otro lado tienes a otro equipo que seguro que estará al máximo de su concentración, El rival tiene calidad y tiene cosas muy bien trabajados. Tiene un perfil muy visible y, aúnque no conozco a su entrenador, no trabaja mal. Tiene identidad y es un partido que tenemos que estar al 100%" Terreno de juego "Espero que esté bien, porque puede ser una de las cuestiones de lesiones. No puedo quejarme porque cada uno tiene lo que puede. Si está bien, mejor para todos, y si no está bien, es porque no pueden. No tienen las condiciones de la liga. Yo no puedo hablar de eso" Posibilidad para el filial "La puerta está abierta siempre. No se abre para un partido de copa. Hay una relación muy cercana y no es la primera vez que ellos han venido a entrenar con nosotros. Han trabajado muchas veces, más de 50 entrenamientos. Hay algunos que vendrán con el equipo, aunque hay una regla que solo puedes jugar con cuatro canteranos. Los que irán, lo merecen" Situación de Marc Santos "Él está más que preparado para jugar. Entrena con nosotros y no hay ninguna sesión de que él sea el peor. Ha sido porque yo he pensado en él primero, pero después miré otros espacios que nos podrían dar una cosa diferente. Después de mirar que no ha ido bien, piensas que podrías ir a por Marc. Lo dije porque me preguntaron por la juventud de la plantilla y yo le contesté que tenía la idea de meter a Marc. No miro la edad de los jugadores. Fue por una cuestión táctica. Para mí el jugador no tiene quince años. Es uno más de la plantilla. Entró en un partido de la liga y él, no lo hizo mal. En pretemporada, como extremo y como "10" estuvo bien" Portero de liga y otro de copa "No hay un portero para la liga y otro para la copa. Hay tres porteros y pueden jugar l aliga y la copa. No se si terminaré el año con Ryan jugando la copa y Primo, jugando la liga. Conmigo en el fútbol no hay posiciones hechas, y el año pasado lo visteis. No hay posiciones que son de un jugador. En todas las posiciones manda el mérito. Los jugadores ya saben lo que tienen que mejorar, porque lo trabajamos, y no hay ninguna posición, ni portero ni delantero ni extremos de copa ni liga. Depende del trabajo" Visita de Espí "Está bien y está contento. El club lo trata muy bien. Está muy contento con su staff. Son buenas personas y trabajan muy bien. Continúa humilde como siempre y yo pienso que llegará muy lejos. Estamos contentos con su visita, al igual que Pampín, que vino antes de irse. Espí es más mediático pero la sensaciones son la misma que otros jugadores"

articles.title: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around
articles.summary: Man Utd's under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick being given the opportunity to turn current situation around with the 13-time Premier League winners currently on an eight-game winless run in all competitions and one point above the relegation zone
articles.body:
The under-pressure United head coach was thought to be on the brink after Sunday's crushing 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, but he and the players are being given the chance to turn the current situation around.

United's director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, were at Carrington discussing Carrick's future on Monday. It is understood they had already been considering alternatives for the head coach role.

However, Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision has been taken to give him at least one more match. Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are among the contenders to replace him if he is sacked.

United go to Stamford Bridge on Saturday lunchtime without a win in eight matches in all competitions. The 13-time Premier League winners sit one point and two places above the relegation zone.

Following the trip to Chelsea, United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday November 3 and Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday November 8, live on Sky Sports .

Matchgoing fans at Old Trafford showed their support for former United midfielder Carrick before booing the players in a reflection of where their frustrations lie.

Carrick dropped captain Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth after he criticised the coaching staff's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como. He will now have to decide whether to bring the Portuguese back into the side at Chelsea.

Xabi Alonso's side are currently fifth, six points better off than United after eight matches, after losing 2-0 at home to rivals Tottenham at Stamford Bridge.

Carrick was initially appointed as United boss in January 2026 on a contract until the end of the season, following Ruben Amorim's sacking earlier in that campaign. He delivered a brilliant run of results, winning 12 of 17 matches to earn a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

He was made permanent head coach on May 22.

Since Jim Ratcliffe became a part owner of United to take control of the football operations nearly three years ago, he has overseen the mid-season sackings of Amorim and Erik ten Hag.

Analysis: Man Utd 'delaying the inevitable' with Carrick

"I'm staggered. We all expected this to be the end for Carrick. The mood music around the club, the reaction of the supporters at Old Trafford - they clearly thought it was the end.

"It's a real surprise. I'm not sure this does anything for his standing. This isn't a vote of confidence. It doesn't feel like Man Utd are saying, 'He's our man, we're sticking with him'.

"I felt for Carrick going onto the training pitch [on Tuesday] and trying to coach and work with Bruno Fernandes, who publicly criticised his tactics. How can Carrick be among that group and for it to be successful and harmonious?

"It's an impossible situation for Carrick and feels like it's delaying the inevitable."

Your views on Carrick being given more time

Jimbo: The correct decision. To remove Michael Carrick would have been another win for player power.

Blev: If I was Carrick I would resign and leave on my terms rather than get dragged through the mud. It's inevitable what's going to happen.

CeeJay: It's about time fans backed the manager. We'd all be moaning if it was another manager down, so what's it to be?

Jas: It's all about standards. Carrick carries himself with class and integrity. Someone needs to hold those values at the club. Otherwise it's an egotistical board and egotistical players left to sort it out.

PapaGino: I couldn't be happier that Carrick remains in charge. The players need to be held to account. Carrick obviously has the club's best interest at heart. Now it's time to see the same commitment from the players.

Connor D: The fact of the matter is it doesn't matter who comes in, the club is rotten to its core.

JordanK94: Silence from the club is deafening. Another season wasted and another ex-player being dragged through the mud.

Dave: Wilcox and the CEO should go, not Carrick.

articles.title: Michael Carrick to stay in charge of Man Utd for Chelsea game
articles.summary: Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their trip to Chelsea this weekend.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their trip to Chelsea this weekend.

Sources have told BBC Sport that the 45-year-old will be given the opportunity to turn things around at Old Trafford following a dismal start to the campaign.

Carrick oversaw training on Tuesday morning, as United look to end a run of eight matches without a win in all competitions when they visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Sunday's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford plunged Carrick's future into doubt, with United sitting one place above the relegation zone.

It is understood United's hierarchy have explored the possibility of replacing Carrick, with ex-Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann under consideration.

But sources have told BBC Sport that the former Middlesbrough manager will not only take charge against Chelsea but will also be given a chance to revive the club's fortunes on the pitch.

Carrick took interim charge in January following Ruben Amorim's departure and he was rewarded with the permanent job in May after securing Champions League qualification with an impressive run that resulted in them finishing third.

But United's form has collapsed this term, with Carrick's side winning just one of their eight Premier League matches so far this season.

Defender Lisandro Martinez criticised the club's board for a lack of investment following United's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League earlier this month.

Captain Bruno Fernandes then took aim at Carrick's tactics following a humiliating 4-1 loss against Como in their next Champions League fixture.

The Portuguese was dropped to the bench for Sunday's loss to Bournemouth, and remained an unused substitute.

United supporters chanted Carrick's name as the former England international made his way to the tunnel after the match, but quickly directed boos at the players once Carrick had made his way off the pitch.

Carrick gestured towards the Stretford End as they chanted his name after the match.

"It wasn't a farewell from me," Carrick said on Sky Sports.

"I've mixed emotions, I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment.

"Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way. To have that connection with the supporters it's mixed emotions, it'll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support.

"The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough."

Carrick was at also United's training ground on Monday morning, despite the first team being given the day off.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada were both pictured arriving at the club's training ground on Monday, with Carrick leaving at about 17:00 GMT.

Howe, 48, is available after leaving Newcastle United last summer but any club that hires the Englishman will have to pay a multi-million pound compensation package to the Magpies after he resigned from his post with three years remaining on his deal.

Nagelsmann, 39, resigned as Germany boss following their quarter-final exit at the 2026 World Cup and is aware of United's interest in him.

Sources have also indicated Aston Villa boss Unai Emery is admired at United, but the fact he is under contract would complicate any move for the Spaniard.

Questions over Carrick remain - analysis

Manchester United might be trying to pass this off as business as usual but the reality is anything but.

The mere fact there was no clarification around Carrick's future on Monday - both before and after he was at the training ground to watch an Under-21 game his son Jacey was part of, or on Tuesday after his 07:30 arrival at Carrington and the 11:00 training start time, fuels theories and speculation, which just adds to the air of uncertainty.

Carrick will be in charge at Stamford Bridge, but what about Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and Aston Villa after that?

Given the woeful nature of their last two performances, how will United's players respond at Chelsea when the spotlight on them is so fierce? Can Carrick drag a performance out of them? Has he made his peace with skipper Bruno Fernandes?

Is director of football Jason Wilcox safe? There are still so many unanswered questions.

Last season's win at Stamford Bridge was one of the key results in securing Carrick the head coach's job permanently. Will the next trip there be the start of a brighter future or mark the end of his tenure?

articles.title: Soccer Star Kylian Mbappé Apologizes for Apparent Reference to Mao as a 'Dictator'
articles.summary: BEIJING (AP) — Soccer star Kylian Mbappé apologized for comments in which he apparently referred to Mao Zedong, the founding leader of Communist China, as a dictator, after facing backlash and losing brand deals with at least three different Chinese companies.
articles.body:
BEIJING (AP) — Soccer star Kylian Mbappé apologized for comments in which he apparently referred to Mao Zedong, the founding leader of Communist China, as a dictator, after facing backlash and losing brand deals with at least three different Chinese companies.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement Tuesday.

"I apologize to everyone my words have upset," he said. "This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry."

Mbappé's face appears in ads across China, from subway stations to inside elevators.

Beverage maker Dongpeng, dairy giant Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground said in similarly worded statements Tuesday that they were ending agreements with the soccer star, each saying they oppose "any words and actions that hurt national sentiment."

The companies did not specify what prompted their decisions, but they released their statements after a clip that appeared to show Mbappé being interviewed ahead of going on the French online talk show "The Bridge" circulated on X.

In the video, Mbappé is asked about his favorite meme of himself, and the soccer star replies that it was "a video someone made of a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator" before the video shows an altered image depicting Mbappé's face on the blue-suited body of Mao Zedong.

China Media Group also said that it has suspended broadcasts of matches in the Spanish league, La Liga, and other games featuring the French soccer star, and removed advertisements featuring him. The media conglomerate demanded an apology from Mbappé and his club, Real Madrid.

The Spanish league was quick to try to protect its television business in China. It said in a statement that it "deeply regrets the offense caused to Chinese fans by Kylian Mbappé's recent comments. These remarks were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga."

The league said it would create a "communication protocol" for its players and clubs while working with stakeholders in China to prevent any future incidents.

Soccer fans online jokingly call the star — who's said to overshadow many of his teammates and even the teams he plays on — a dictator, and memes showing him as Mao or other autocratic leaders are widely circulated.

Mao Zedong was a revolutionary who led the Communist Party during its crucial early days, winning a civil war against the ruling Nationalist Party in China, and then founding the modern day People's Republic of China.

Mao is revered by many even today. However, he leaves behind a complex legacy of authoritarian rule, having led campaigns like the Great Leap Forward, an industrialization project which led to a famine that killed an estimated 30 million people.

China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said in response to a question about the controversy that "words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."

Social media platform RedNote joined the criticism, saying in a separate statement that the company had a content partnership with Mbappé that ended on Dec. 31, 2024, and that it would "remove related promotional materials." It expressed opposition to "any conduct that hurts national sentiment."

Mbappé's account on RedNote was banned from accepting new followers Tuesday.

Mbappé has featured in advertising campaigns in China for products from electrolyte drinks to milk and cheese. In one commercial for Dongpeng, Mbappé delivers a slogan in Chinese; in an ad for Mengniu, he appears alongside Argentine soccer star Lionel Messi.

On Chinese social media, there were comments criticizing the soccer star.

The hashtags "Dongpeng ends partnership with Mbappé" and "Several brands end partnerships with Mbappé" topped Weibo's trending list. "Football fans boycott Mbappé" was also trending, with some users expressing anger at his remarks or telling him not to come to China.

articles.title: Modric siempre sale a cuenta: "Si tenemos que perder algo, prefiero que sea sin balón"
articles.standfirst: Su asistencia contra Udinese le convirtió en el jugador mayor de 40 años con más pases de gol (4) registrados en la Serie A en más de dos décadas
articles.summary: Su asistencia contra Udinese le convirtió en el jugador mayor de 40 años con más pases de gol (4) registrados en la Serie A en más de dos décadas
articles.body: "Cuando llegas aquí, lo percibes. Se respira la historia del Milan. Esa fue una de las razones por las que elegí venir", confesaba Luka Modric en MARCA el pasado mes de septiembre. Reconocía que su objetivo era "hacerlo mejor que el año pasado". Pasa el tiempo... pero su magia se mantiene intacta. La llegada de Rúben Amorim al banquillo de San Siro ha matizado ligeramente su rol. Allegri, desde el primer día, tuvo claro que debía ser el 'cerebro' del equipo y, protegido por otros dos interiores de mucho recorrido, lo reconvirtió en un 'regista' que se erigió en el segundo jugador de la Serie A con mayor volumen de pases precisos (2.473)... registrando un 90.4% de acierto. En cierta medida, a sus ya más de 41 años, le venía relativamente bien esa propuesta más parsimoniosa y, sobre todo, reactiva sin balón. Con Amorim, se esperaba que el Milan 'mutase' hacia una propuesta más dinámica en la que, con el cambio al 1-3-4-3, Modric —centrocampista de la Serie A que menos distancia a alta intensidad (349.3) promedia— se vería bastante más expuesto. Poco a poco, están comenzando a cambiar hábitos... y se comprueba al medir que el conjunto 'rossonero' ha pasado de ser el 17º equipo que menos pases permite a su rival al noveno. La sustitución al descanso contra la Lazio con 2-0 abajo antes del parón levantó sospechas sobre que su presencia podía estar impidiendo transitar hacia ese modelo. Ahora bien, la realidad es que el Milan no tiene un jugador con su pie y criterio en la organización que se le acerque a Modric. Es, de hecho, el segundo centrocampista de la Serie A que más pases largos promedia (10.4) y el que más jugadores supera desde sus envíos (13.4). Además, también está teniendo incidencia en los resultados. "Modric no puede presionar todo el tiempo, pero siempre tiene el ritmo del partido en sus manos y entiende el juego mejor que nadie", expresaba Amorim. "Como entrenador, tengo que elegir. Quizás, perdemos algo en la presión. Pero, con Modric en el campo, tenemos más control. Si tenemos que perder algo, prefiero que sea sin balón". Titular en los tres partidos de Serie A disputados después del parón, asistió a Rabiot en el empate contra el Sassuolo y volvió a hacer lo propio con Christian Pulisic para comenzar a sembrar el triunfo frente a Udinese. Según los registros de 'OPTA', Modric ha superado a Ibrahimovic como el jugador mayor de 40 años con más asistencias (4) en la Liga italiana desde la temporada 04-05. "Cuando Modric tiene el balón, ese es mi trabajo: atacar el espacio a la espalda de la defensa. Vi que había metros, me metí, hice un buen control y marqué", detallaba Christian Pulisic sobre la asistencia que le regaló desde el centro del campo a balón parado un Luka Modric que, por primera vez en toda la temporada, completó los 90'. Fue, además, el segundo jugador que más veces (103) entró en contacto con la pelota y también el segundo que más pases (84/91) con éxito completó a lo largo del encuentro. El único que le superó en ambas facetas fue Ardon Jashari, su socio en la sala de máquinas. "Creo que hay un buen 'feeling' entre nosotros. Nos entendemos bien… Me gusta mucho jugar a su lado". "He hablado con él dos veces y, si hace falta, volveré a hacerlo. Es un punto fundamental. Quizá no juegue todos los partidos, pero contamos con él. Quiero que se quede. Hablé con Luka y, si hace falta… iré a buscarlo en persona. Le quiero con nosotros esta temporada", expuso Amorim durante la pretemporada. Tener a Modric siempre saldrá a cuenta.

articles.title: Mensaje de resiliencia de Cancelo
articles.standfirst: El internacional publica una imagen suya en blanco y negro junto a la canción 'Yo creo en mí'
articles.summary: El internacional publica una imagen suya en blanco y negro junto a la canción 'Yo creo en mí'
articles.body: Cancelo ha vuelto a recurrir a las redes sociales para lanzar un mensaje de confianza. El internacional portugués publicó este martes una imagen suya acompañada de un trozo muy significativo de la canción, Yo creo en mí, cuya letra refleja la capacidad de superación. El Barcelona ha perdido los dos últimos compromisos, contra PSG y Real Madrid. No es la primera vez que el lateral portugués utiliza sus perfiles sociales para dar un paso al frente. Después de las críticas recibidas tras el encuentro en el Parque de los Príncipes, Cancelo ya dejó un mensaje contundente en el que defendía la dificultad de competir al máximo nivel. "Desde la grada todo el mundo es especialista y me gustaría verlos entrar en el campo y aguantar la presión", escribió. En aquella publicación, el defensa acompañó su reflexión con la canción They Don't Care About Us (no les importamos), de Michael Jackson. Este martes, Cancelo ha vuelto a pronunciarse a través de las redes sociales. En esta ocasión, el portugués compartió una fotografía suya de espaldas, en blanco y negro, acompañada de la canción Yo creo en mí, de El Armenio. La capacidad de sobreponerse a las adversidades es el centro de su mensaje. "Ese soy yo, un lobo de verdad. No me rindo nunca, yo nací para ganar. Ese soy yo, con hambre de más, si caigo al suelo me vuelvo a levantar. Yo creo en mí, no voy a parar, tengo fuego dentro y palabra real. He pasado noches sin saber qué hacer, con la mente rota pero de pie otra vez. Nadie vio mi duda, nadie vio mi presión, solo vieron mi fuerza cuando salió el lobo. Quiero dinero, quiero respeto, mirarme al espejo y sentirme completo. Quiero ser grande, dejar señal, pero sin vender mi alma", añade", dice la letra escogida por el futbolista. Aunque Cancelo no puso ningún texto en su publicación, solo con la imagen y la canción, el luso volvió a mandar un mensaje de resiliencia, de sobreponerse a los malos resultados y de fortaleza mental.

articles.title: How 'anti-superstar' Harry Kane defied doubters to achieve Ballon d'Or greatness
articles.summary: Harry Kane is the humble 'anti-superstar' who defied doubters to achieve Ballon d'Or greatness, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
Harry Kane has taken the scenic route to the Ballon d'Or - a road littered with doubts and diversions, but one that eventually led to the ultimate destination: being crowned as the world's best player.

The 33-year-old's glory at the London Palladium on Monday is fitting reward for an exemplary career that has seen records fall at his feet for England, Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich.

Kane is England's top goalscorer with 91 goals. He has 125 England caps, joint-highest with Peter Shilton. He is Spurs' record scorer with 280 goals in 435 appearances. He scored a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025–26 season.

This is the Kane of recent vintage, the world-class striker and complete footballer who beat Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappe, as well as Spain's teenage Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, to the sport's biggest personal honour.

Kane's humility has seen him described as an 'anti-superstar' and his achievement has been commended both inside and outside the football world.

One post on social media from Kane as he celebrated the greatest moment of his career said it all: "Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise."

And yet, Kane's journey was not always smooth.

It was one that started with loan moves around the lower divisions with Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City before he developed into a great for club and country.

The same Kane sat on the bench on loan at Leicester City – alongside future England team-mate Jamie Vardy – when the Foxes lost a dramatic Championship play-off at Watford in May 2013.

Kane went through hard schools and hard times away from his more familiar environment at Spurs, joining Orient on loan as a 17-year-old in January 2011, playing 18 games with nine starts and scoring five goals.

He joined Millwall in similar circumstances a year later, with some behind the scenes at Spurs fearing the traditionally hostile atmosphere at the New Den might intimidate the teenager, but he acquitted himself well, scoring nine goals in 24 starts.

Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend

Tributes pour in as Kane wins Ballon d'Or - reaction & your views

Former Spurs manager Tim Sherwood said: "I used to watch Harry a lot at Millwall and it was an intimidating atmosphere. I remember overhearing one of our scouts come and talk to Harry Redknapp - who was Spurs manager at the time - and say: 'We need to get Harry Kane out of Millwall, it's no good for him there'.

"I went straight in and said: 'This is the perfect atmosphere for him'."

Kane made his Spurs debut in August 2012 before a spell at Norwich City, where he failed to score in three starts and suffered a serious foot injury.

It was an unhappy time but Chris Hughton, the former Spurs defender who was manager at Carrow Road, said: "What I saw in him was a desire to do well. Did I see him having the mobility and flexibility he has in his game now? Probably not. He was a very good finisher. He would stay out after training for half an hour every day, left foot, right foot."

Next stop was Leicester City between February and May 2013, when he made five starts and scored two goals, a stint best remembered for that dramatic Championship play-off game when Troy Deeney scored for Watford to send them to Wembley seconds after Anthony Knockaert's penalty was saved by Manuel Almunia.

Kane was not even selected in Leicester's starting line-up, only being sent on after 61 minutes. And who was alongside him on the bench? Vardy, who later won the Premier league with the Foxes and played alongside Kane for England.

He later admitted this was a time of self-doubt, saying: "That was probably the time in my career where it was the hardest - I was 19 and I was thinking, 'If I can't play for Norwich or for Leicester, even in the Championship, then how I am going to get back and play for Tottenham?'"

Ranking England's Ballon d'Or winners - how does Kane compare?

Quiz: Kane and who else? Name every men's Ballon d'Or winner

It is testimony to Kane's strength of character, even as a youngster, that he not only returned to Spurs but left for Bayern Munich in August 2023 as one of their greatest ever players.

Even at Spurs, Kane's superb record always carried the qualification that he never won a trophy, a stick used to unfairly beat a player whose remarkable consistency and approach marked him down as the consummate professional.

Kane has put that right spectacularly at Bayern, winning the Bundesliga twice, the move propelling him to the level of global superstar, giving him the profile and platform to win the Ballon d'Or - the first English player to win the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001 and the fifth overall.

Former England midfielder Danny Murphy told BBC Sport recently: "He's a born goalscorer. He's a super professional. He's technically brilliant. He's been an absolute credit to himself and his family in the way he's conducted himself and the longevity he's had in his career."

There is still that one space on his roll of honour, namely success with England after losses in two Euros finals and two World Cup semi-final defeats, but who would bet against Kane being fit and motivated enough to have one last crack at Euro 2028 in the UK and Ireland.

Kane is now at the peak of his powers and fitness, not just a goalscoring machine but the complete player capable of dropping deep into midfield to play the sort of breathtaking defence splitting pass exemplified by Alphonso Davies' goal against Arsenal in the recent Champions League game.

One of Kane's illustrious predecessors in England's number nine shirt, Alan Shearer, told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It was so well deserved because he hasn't had things all his own way. He's had to go round it the hard way. He had to start off the hard way by someone telling him, 'You're not quite good enough, you're going to have to work a lot harder to get to where you want to'.

"He did that. He went out on loan and worked harder than anyone else. He's got to the very, very top and now he's the best player in the world and that's what dedication does for you. It's a message to everyone.

"Harry said it in his speech - that if you're told you're not good enough, then go and try again and work harder. He did that and look where he is now. He's been scoring goals at a phenomenal rate for so many years now and he deserved it."

Shearer added: "I think the best thing for me is how humble Harry is. Footballers are like movie stars nowadays. You see them walking down the red carpet and some of them are in sunglasses when it's pitch black and eight o'clock at night. Harry is just normal, as normal as they come."

Once the celebrations die down, it will be back to business for the humble superstar, with Bayern playing Magdeburg in the German DFB Pokal second round on Wednesday before the big home fixture against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday evening.

Kane's career has not been without its obstacles but he remains as focused as ever to conquer whatever is placed in front of him by Bayern Munich and England.

articles.title: Manso pide más diálogo con los árbitros: "Parece que te intimidan con la mirada"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Andorra lamenta la poca accesibilidad de los colegiados y admite que prefiere no profundizar en sus críticas para evitar una posible sanción
articles.summary: El técnico del Andorra lamenta la poca accesibilidad de los colegiados y admite que prefiere no profundizar en sus críticas para evitar una posible sanción
articles.body: Carles Manso ha mostrado su malestar con la actitud de los árbitros tras la derrota del Andorra ante el Burgos. Más allá de las decisiones concretas, el técnico tricolor ha lamentado las dificultades para comunicarse con los colegiados durante los partidos. "Tengo ganas de hablar, pero no puedo hacerlo porque entonces me sancionarán", ha señalado en rueda de prensa, antes de matizar que su queja no se dirige a todos los árbitros. "Parece que te intimidan con la mirada, que te quieren cortar en todo momento y están muy poco accesibles a la hora de hablar con ellos", ha añadido. En este sentido, el de Terrassa ha reclamado una mayor predisposición al diálogo y ha defendido que los entrenadores deberían poder pedir explicaciones sin temor a ser expulsados: "Creo que pueden ser un poco más receptivos, por lo menos para explicarnos sus decisiones. Y no tener que callar por tener que callar, porque al final tienen la amenaza de expulsarte". Así pues, el entrenador catalán ha preferido no extenderse más en sus valoraciones, lamentando que, "si no, probablemente la semana que viene no pueda estar". Respecto al penalti por mano de Martí Vilà que ha supuesto el tercer gol del conjunto burgalés, Manso ha explicado que desde el banquillo consideraban que el defensa tenía inicialmente el brazo muy pegado al cuerpo y que el balón le había tocado antes en otra zona. También ha señalado que el movimiento posterior del jugador respondía a su intención de dejar pasar la pelota. "Creíamos que podía ser una acción revisable, que al final no ha sido así", ha concluido.

articles.title: Otorbi renueva con el Valencia hasta 2031
articles.standfirst: El club ejecuta de forma anticipada la ampliación prevista en el contrato del extremo, una de las grandes promesas de la cantera valencianista
articles.summary: El club ejecuta de forma anticipada la ampliación prevista en el contrato del extremo, una de las grandes promesas de la cantera valencianista
articles.body: El Valencia ha asegurado la continuidad de David Otorbi hasta junio de 2031. El club ha ejecutado de manera anticipada la ampliación contractual que contemplaba el acuerdo firmado por el futbolista y blinda así a una de las principales promesas de su cantera. La firma de la renovación se ha celebrado este martes en la Ciudad Deportiva de Paterna en un acto privado. Junto al futbolista han estado presentes sus padres y su representante, Nacho Gallart, además de responsables del club valencianista. Otorbi, que sigue dando pasos en su progresión dentro de la estructura del Valencia, ha alternado durante esta temporada participaciones con el primer equipo y el Valencia Mestalla, consolidándose como uno de los jóvenes con mayor proyección de la entidad. La renovación supone una muestra de confianza del club en el desarrollo deportivo del atacante y refuerza su apuesta por el talento formado en la Academia. El extremo valencianista se convirtió la pasada campaña en el jugador más joven en debutar con el primer equipo del Valencia en partido oficial y ha mantenido desde entonces una evolución que le ha permitido permanecer en la dinámica habitual de la primera plantilla. El crecimiento de Otorbi también ha despertado interés fuera de España. MARCA informó recientemente de que el Newcastle había seguido de cerca las evoluciones del futbolista y que emisarios del club inglés estuvieron presentes en El Sardinero durante el encuentro entre el Valencia Mestalla y el Racing para observar al jugador. El seguimiento se enmarca dentro del interés habitual de clubes europeos por algunos de los jóvenes talentos con mayor proyección del fútbol español. Pendiente del alcance de su lesión La renovación llega en un momento en el que el futbolista permanece a la espera de conocer el alcance exacto de la lesión muscular sufrida el pasado sábado frente al Villarreal. Otorbi tuvo que abandonar el terreno de juego tras notar molestias y está pendiente de las pruebas médicas y del correspondiente parte oficial del Valencia. A falta de confirmación por parte del club, las primeras previsiones apuntan a un periodo de baja superior al mes, por lo que el extremo se perdería varios compromisos en un tramo importante de la temporada. La lesión interrumpe temporalmente su progresión deportiva, aunque la renovación refuerza la confianza del Valencia en su presente y en su proyección a largo plazo

articles.title: Hearts: Harry Milne out for season as injury woes continue
articles.summary: Heart of Midlothian defender Harry Milne's season is over after he sustains an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, head coach Wouter Vrancken confirms.
articles.body:
Heart of Midlothian left-back Harry Milne's season is over after he sustained an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, head coach Wouter Vrancken has confirmed.

The 29-year-old, who has become an integral part of the Tynecastle side over the past year, suffered the injury during a training session in preparation for last Thursday's Conference League defeat away to Trabzonspor.

After being voted into the PFA Scotland Premiership team of the year last season, Milne was named one of Hearts' vice-captains by Vrancken in July.

"Harry is unfortunate, with his season finished," the Hearts boss said as he faces going into Wednesday's home encounter with Rangers without eight first-team players.

"It was an ACL, as I expected. There was a bit of hope, but now it's just unlucky for him. It was hard for him, but he has made peace with it."

Hearts chairman calls for greater transparency on key decisions

Hearts enjoy rare away win as Motherwell gloom lingers

Visit our Hearts page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Milne is among a long list of Hearts absentees, with Vrancken also confirming fellow defenders Stuart Findlay and Christian Borchgrevink face more time on the sidelines.

The Belgian coach expects Blair Spittal to return before Christmas but says "it's difficult to see" fellow midfielder Tom Renaud being back by then.

Hearts travelled to Motherwell on Sunday with a depleted squad but managed to grind out a hard-fought 2-0 victory .

Vrancken says his squad will be unchanged for the visit of Rangers, which marks the return of manager Derek McInnes following his departure from Hearts in June.

"We have the same focus as we've had on a few occasions already this season," the Belgian added as his side look to narrow the four-point gap between themselves and second-top Rangers.

"Focus on what you have to do on the pitch, because we want to win the game and get the result, even with the injuries.

"We want good confidence with the players on the pitch and in the squad and to keep the belief there.

"Negative emotions, or emotions in general, that are not focused on what we have to do, don't bring anything extra to the game. There's always noise you have to block out or avoid."

articles.title: Aranbarri: "Hemos puesto el foco en la agresividad y en el trabajo sin balón"

articles.summary: El técnico tiene detectados los males del Eibar en su última derrota en Córdoba
articles.body: El Eibar quiere aprovechar el duelo de Copa ante el CD Pamplona para volver a la senda del triunfo después de tres jornadas sin ganar en Liga y un último encuentro en Córdoba que le dejó muy mal sabor de boca. Jokin Aranbarri es consciente de la necesidad de recuperar el mejor nivel competitivo tras firmar en el Nuevo Arcángel un partido muy alejado de lo que quiere de su equipo. "Somos conscientes de que a partir del minuto 25 estuvimos mal y, desde el día siguiente, hemos puesto el foco en eso: en la agresividad y en el trabajo sin balón. El equipo ha dado un paso adelante a la hora de sentir las cosas, porque para mí el primer paso siempre es sentirlas de verdad. Cuando veo al equipo y hablamos, creo que siente de verdad cuándo hace las cosas bien y cuándo las hace mal. Y ese es el primer paso. El segundo es tener claro en qué cosas hemos estado bien y qué necesitamos mejorar". El técnico armero cuenta con numerosas bajas y volverá a tirar de varios canteranos para completar la convocatoria. "Es una buena oportunidad y hay que dejar claro que no es un regalo. Creo que cada jugador se lo está ganando de verdad. El filial está haciendo una muy buena temporada y creo que Iñigo y su staff están realizando un gran trabajo. Hay buenos jugadores y, cada vez que vienen futbolistas del filial a los entrenamientos o a los partidos, siempre suman. Tienen calidad y potencial, y va a haber oportunidades porque se las están ganando". Aranbarri no se fía de un rival al que ha visto en directo para poder conocer mejor. "Si están jugando la Copa es porque llevan mucho tiempo haciendo cosas bien. No hace falta decir que tenemos el máximo respeto por ellos. He estado viendo presencialmente un partido porque me gusta comprobar a qué velocidad juegan y la capacidad de cada jugador. Me han gustado muchas cosas de lo que están haciendo. Es verdad que no están sacando los partidos adelante en cuanto a resultados, pero, por todo lo que hacen bien, creo que son un equipo muy peligroso".

articles.title: Was the Ballon d'Or in London the most chaotic?
articles.summary: It was the first time the Ballon d'Or had been held in London in its 70-year history - but the event was not plain sailing. BBC Sport assesses a chaotic night.
articles.body:
It was the first time the Ballon d'Or had been held in London in its 70-year history, with organisers choosing the iconic London Palladium as the venue.

Despite the perfect homecoming for Harry Kane on Monday night, the rest of the event was not plain sailing.

Did the organisers give away the winners early or was it just a simple mix-up? Why was the ceremony delayed and why was the audience booing?

BBC Sport assesses a chaotic night in central London.

London traffic can cause issues on any day but unfortunately for the Ballon d'Or organisers, they chose to hold a major event just a stone's throw from Oxford Street on the same day the famous shopping area was made traffic-free.

That, coupled with large crowds at the event entrance, meant significant numbers of guests were delayed and the start had to be pushed back by 45 minutes.

Once it did get under way, a rowdy and boisterous audience sat through a ceremony that lasted nearly two and a half hours. On a number of occasions, hosts Kate Scott and Thierry Henry had to briefly pause proceedings while people shouted the names of players in the audience and there were several instances of booing during commercial breaks.

After Kane and Alexia Putellas had been crowned the winners in the two main categories, they then spoke to the world's media in separate press conferences.

Journalists were able to put questions to Putellas but only men were selected to ask Kane a question, with several female journalists having their attempts seemingly ignored.

The Ballon d'Or team has since apologised.

How Kane defied doubters to become world's best

Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend

Hundreds of people gathered outside the London Palladium to try to get a glimpse of the biggest stars in football on the red carpet. A security perimeter of metal fencing and barricades had been erected to try to keep those without a ticket out.

But the BBC Sport team witnessed those barriers being scaled, broken and ripped down and several people being evicted by security after making their way through.

The atmosphere at times was tense, with footage on social media appearing to show fans clashing with security and police.

The BBC has approached the Metropolitan Police for comment.

The confusion and chaos began hours before the ceremony had even started, after the official Ballon d'Or website published an article declaring Kane as the winner of the men's award.

Further digging revealed similar articles had been published about some of the other favourites to win the men's and women's awards, including Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and London City Lionesses' Putellas.

Was it a genuine mistake? Or a case of trying to divert people's attention from the initial Kane announcement? Which of course turned out to be true.

A Ballon d'Or spokesperson told BBC Sport last night they were "inadvertently published online".

"These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings," the spokesperson said.
