articles.title: Utah Apologizes to Pat McAfee for Social Media Video After 'College GameDay' Star's Comments
articles.summary: The fallout from Pat McAfee's comments about Utah on Saturday's episode of College GameDay has continued, with the University of Utah issuing an apology to the ESPN personality.
articles.body:
The fallout from Pat McAfee's comments about Utah on Saturday's episode of College GameDay has continued, with the University of Utah issuing an apology to the ESPN personality.

In a statement released on Monday, the school took "full accountability" for the social media video at the center of the discussion and noted university officials reached out to McAfee to "sincerely apologize" for the situation.

The situation began on Saturday with the ESPN pregame show broadcasting from Salt Lake City for the Houston-Utah matchup. During the final segment when the panelists make their picks, McAfee closed his remarks by saying to the crowd in attendance, "I'll never see you again, hopefully."

McAfee further addressed the situation on Monday's episode of his ESPN show by saying he felt "uncomfortable" about a social media video of Utah Students doing a McAfee impression that the university later posted on its official Instagram page (h/t The Athletic's Chris Vannini ).

"Did not enjoy University of Utah," McAfee said at the start of his show. "You know why I didn't like it mostly? Right before I go out there, I see the University of Utah's Instagram page. They put out, do an impression of Pat McAfee, and one kid goes, 'Ah, he's corny.' Another kid calls me creepy. If these kids would have done this on their own blogs, all good. Everybody's taking shots at me, anyways, for everything. I get it. If the two ladies that were hosting that put that out on their own blog, I'd be OK with it. You're allowed to do what you do.

"The university puts that out? Like as I'm about to go out and do an infomercial for the place? And then I'm walking in front of thousands of these people. This is how the university feels about it? It's an uncomfortable feeling."

The school later deleted the video from its account. Saturday marked the seventh time College GameDay has broadcast from Salt Lake City prior to a Utes home game. It was the first time since November 2025 for a Cincinnati-Utah matchup.

Utah defeated Houston 21-13 at Rice–Eccles Stadium on Saturday night to improve to 7-0 this season.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola drops lineup hints ahead of Chelsea and Arsenal games
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola Backs Liverpool Rotation as Chelsea Cup Tie Tests Squad DepthAndoni Iraola has made his position clear. Liverpool will keep rotating, and he se...
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola Backs Liverpool Rotation as Chelsea Cup Tie Tests Squad Depth

Andoni Iraola has made his position clear. Liverpool will keep rotating, and he sees no reason to apologise for it.

With Chelsea arriving at Anfield in the Carabao Cup before another major test against Arsenal, the Liverpool head coach has doubled down on a selection policy that has defined his season so far. He has not named the same starting XI in back to back matches, and across the last seven games he has changed at least three players every time.

That pattern is set to continue. Iraola described rotation as "almost mandatory," which tells you everything about how he views modern fixture congestion.

"There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game, we want to be competitive," he said. "We need to see how the legs are.

"We are – not just in the Carabao Cup, also in the Champions League – trying to make some changes from game to game, because I think it's almost mandatory.

"We want to be in the next round. We've been unlucky in the draw, we are playing Chelsea – they've been unlucky also – but we want to earn the right to be in the draw again.

Liverpool rotation policy built for relentless schedule

This is practical management. Liverpool have played regularly, the games are stacking up, and Iraola is handling it like someone who understands the difference between sentiment and necessity. Top sides competing every three days do not survive by asking the same players to empty themselves repeatedly.

The numbers support him. Liverpool have lost only one of their last 10 matches in all competitions and have won eight of them. The rotation has not disrupted rhythm. If anything, it has protected it.

That matters even more in attack, where the demand is clear, play at full intensity and do it for as long as possible. That only works if legs are fresh.

Iraola put it plainly: "I think it's not that we have a lot of options; we need to rotate.

"Every top team that plays every three days needs to rotate.

"Sometimes they are forced rotations, because you don't have players available and it's more difficult for me.

"Sometimes it's because we consider for the different games we have different demands, and we have to go different tactically.

"But I'm happy because I see everyone is involved and when we've had the need to use someone who was not playing, for one game for 10 minutes, whoever has been there has helped us.

"The more players we can have in a good place, the easier my selection is going to be – even if it's hard in terms of leaving players out.

"I prefer those problems than not having the players ready."

Chelsea Carabao Cup tie offers fringe players a chance

The selection questions are obvious. Liverpool remain without Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Vitezslav Jaros, while Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz are carrying doubts.

Florian Wirtz is expected to be involved after twisting his ankle at the weekend, though starting him would be a risk Iraola may decide is unnecessary.

That opens the door for several squad players. Giorgi Mamardashvili, Joe Gomez, Kostas Tsimikas, Trey Nyoni, James McConnell, Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas all have a realistic chance of starting. Wataru Endo has yet to feature this season but is available, and Federico Chiesa is back fit and pushing for minutes.

Squad depth could define Liverpool season

This is where seasons get shaped. Not in broad declarations, but in whether the second line can carry real weight when the calendar becomes unforgiving.

Iraola clearly believes Liverpool's squad is engaged, prepared and strong enough to absorb change without losing edge. Against Chelsea, that belief gets another test. If Liverpool win, the policy looks smart. If they do not, the logic still holds. Rotation is not a luxury for teams with serious ambitions. It is part of the job.

articles.title: Harry Kane opens up on whether he might return to the Premier League after winning Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: England captain still trails Alan Shearer’s long-standing Premier League goal record by 47 goals
articles.body:
Harry Kane says he has no plans to return to the Premier League to topple Alan Shearer's goalscoring record, and has instead set his sights on winning the Champions League with Bayern Munich and a major trophy with England.

Kane left Tottenham three years ago after scoring 213 Premier League goals, and he remains second on the list of all-time scorers behind Shearer, who scored 260.

The move to Bayern has been vindicated by two Bundesliga titles and a German Cup in his three seasons at the club, having scored 156 goals in 159 games, and his talents have finally been recognised after winning the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday evening.

Asked whether he might want to return to England to overtake Shearer's mark, Kane said: "Not at the moment, not right now. I'm loving life in Munich. Bayern are such a great club. We have an amazing team, a great coach [Vincent Kompany]. So yeah, right now that's where my focus is, and I'm extremely happy, and to be winning awards like this just shows why I made the move in the first place."

Kane is 33 but is determined to keep playing at the highest level into his late 30s, and says his biggest goal is finally winning a trophy with England after a series of near misses over the past eight years.

"There's always ambition, there's always dreams for new achievements, new things. I still have a lot to achieve in this game – the Champions League, from club level, and to win a major trophy with England, it's my number one priority for sure.

"There's so many great things I want to achieve, and I've learned in a career, in life, you don't really have much of a say. You just have to go with the flow, see where it takes you, believe in what you're going to do, like I think making the move, and then just go full gas.

"Right now it's with Munich, and we'll see where that takes me."

Kane spent the evening celebrating with family and friends in London before returning to Munich on an early flight to train with his teammates ahead of a German Cup game on Wednesday.

Kane said he spoke with his manager, Kompany, on the morning of the Ballon d'Or ceremony. Kompany is being treated in hospital for a viral infection after collapsing during a training session.

"He actually phoned me this morning, bright and early at 9am," Kane said. "I was just out of bed, thankfully, so I was able to answer it. He just wanted to wish me all the best, good luck.

"I asked him how he was doing, he said he feels good, he's on the mend. I know he's the type of character who just wants to be back with the team already, he wants to be out on the training field with us, on the bench with us. But it's important that he rests. He's been going through a bit of a tough time with his health recently, and we can hopefully cover it, and the staff can cover it whilst he's not there.

"It will be massive for me to go back to Munich, to see him, all the staff, all my teammates. I've spoken about how much it is theirs as well as it is mine, so just to celebrate with them a little bit will be special."

images.caption: Kane holds the Ballon d'Or trophy at the London Palladium (PA)

articles.title: Harry Kane - How How Ballon d'Or win could boost the Bundesliga
articles.summary: Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or win not only ended a 25-year wait for an English winner of the award but also saw a Bundesliga player win it for the first time since 1996.
articles.body:
England has had to wait a long time for another winner of the Ballon d'Or, with Harry Kane on Monday night becoming the first player from the country to win it for 25 years.

But his success has also been celebrated in Germany with the Bayern Munich striker ending their even longer run without a player from the Bundesliga lifting the coveted trophy.

The last to do so was Matthias Sammer back in 1996 after he had captained Borussia Dortmund to two successive Bundesliga titles.

"Just as Bayern and the Bundesliga benefit from Kane, the reverse is also true," Lothar Matthaus, the most capped German player of all time and 1991 Ballon d'Or winner, said.

"I don't think Kane would've won the Ballon d'Or at any other club he could've joined. He's developed further at Bayern and matured even more.

"He's become a better player there, as he himself said in his speech. At Bayern, he won his very first title, with more to follow - and now he's fulfilled a lifelong dream."

Ranking England's Ballon d'Or winners - how does Kane compare?

Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend

Quiz: Kane and who else? Name every men's Ballon d'Or winner

What it means for Bayern and the Bundesliga

For Kane, the trophy win will have felt special for many reasons on a personal level, having gone through ups and downs in his career to make it to the very top.

But both the Bundesliga and Bayern know how significant it will also be for the league and the club respectively.

After Kane was announced as the Ballon d'Or winner, large images from the Bundesliga were projected on to landmarks across London such as The Strand and Tate Modern, some featuring the words "England Hero. Bundesliga Legend".

For the league, Kane's win will show players that they can come to the Bundesliga and become recognised as the best player in the world, while for Bayern it will show they are capable of attracting the very best talent.

Bundesliga chief executive Marc Lenz said: "Winning the Ballon d'Or is a tremendous recognition of Harry Kane's extraordinary performances - and also a great success for Bayern and the Bundesliga.

"Harry is not only one of the outstanding players of his generation; he combines sporting excellence with tremendous professionalism, commitment and respect for the game. He gives everything for his team and inspires fans around the world.

"He is a fantastic role model for young players and an outstanding ambassador for the Bundesliga.

"This achievement also underlines that the Bundesliga is a stage where the very best players in the world perform at the highest level."

Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen added: "For a player from a German club to win the Ballon d'Or for the first time in 30 years is a strong signal for the Bundesliga," he said.

"Harry is one of the great personalities of world football and a role model to all, far beyond the game."

German journalist Raphael Honigstein said on BBC Radio 5 live that Kane's impact at Bayern has been significant.

"He's made a huge difference," he told BBC Radio 5 live.

"There's the goals but beyond that there is the focus on Bayern that has come from him. After four-and-a-half decades Bayern have a player with international recognition the way Kane has it.

"It is big for the team and big for the club because they always crave that international validation, whether it comes through the European Cup or through these individual trophies.

Kane's win understandably was praised in the German media, with Henning Feindt, Bild editor-in-chief for sport, writing: "He is the biggest star the league could wish for.

"For 30 years [since Matthias Sammer in 1996], no Bundesliga player has won the most coveted trophy in world football. And for 45 years, not a Bayern Munich player has won it [since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge]. The message Kane is sending to all the world's superstars: It's possible in the Bundesliga too."

How Bayern will celebrate Kane's success

Kane celebrated his Ballon d'Or win by partying into the early hours in London with family and friends, and Bayern are planning to mark his triumph when he returns to Munich.

The club have confirmed Kane will be given "a special welcome" before Wednesday's DFB Cup match against Magdeburg at the Allianz Arena, as well as honouring him at the Bundesliga top-of-the-table match against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday.

"This is a proud day for FC Bayern," club president Herbert Hainer said. "Harry Kane can do it all - and he scores goals, goals and more goals.

"He now joins a line with Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Müller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge - that says everything about our history."

BBC Sport Spanish football reporter Elizabeth Conway:

Kane's Ballon d'Or victory has sparked debate in Spain over the relative importance of individual performances and international success in determining football's most prestigious individual award.

Some Spanish journalists and commentators believe that winning the World Cup should carry greater weight in the voting, particularly when players have also demonstrated outstanding individual form.

Unsurprisingly, sections of the Spanish press have argued that Lamine Yamal and other members of Spain's national team had equally compelling claims, given their performances on the international stage.

The debate has also drawn comparisons with 2010, when Lionel Messi won the award ahead of Spain's World Cup-winning midfielders Andres Iniesta and Xavi.

For some Spanish commentators, Kane's victory raises familiar questions about whether success at major international tournaments receives sufficient recognition in the Ballon d'Or voting process.

El Pais captured the tension between individual achievement and team success, writing: "What would have been a historic double escaped: in London, goals prevailed over titles."

The newspaper also highlighted Spain's strong representation at the ceremony, with Spanish players and teams featuring prominently across the awards, eight of which went to Spanish winners.

The result has also attracted criticism from prominent figures in Spanish football. Jose Felix Diaz, editor-in-chief of AS and Spain's sole journalist voter, revealed that he had expected either Yamal or Kylian Mbappe to win.

His position was reflected in an AS headline: "The Messi-Iniesta controversy returns: Spain's only voter says Kane doesn't deserve the Ballon d'Or."

Former Real Madrid midfielder Guti was similarly critical of the outcome, arguing that Mbappe and Lamine Yamal had stronger claims to the award. He questioned the circumstances surrounding the ceremony, saying: "It's quite a coincidence that they take the 70th anniversary Ballon d'Or ceremony to London and someone from London wins it."

Guti also suggested that Kane himself had not expected to win, pointing to his reaction when his name was announced as evidence that he had anticipated Yamal or Mbappe finishing ahead of him.

Nevertheless, opinion in Spain naturally will favour players in their national team and the majority of press acknowledge Kane is a deserving winner.

articles.title: Mike Norvell revisits the call that changed FSU’s Miami loss
articles.summary: Mike Norvell discussed his conversation with ACC officiating supervisor Gary Patterson after the controversial holding call in FSU's loss to Miami.
articles.body:
One week after blasting the officiating at the end of Florida State 's loss to Miami, Mike Norvell offered a more measured perspective following another conversation with ACC Supervisor of Football Officials Gary Patterson.

Norvell said Monday that he respects the way Patterson handled their discussion and understands that mistakes are part of officiating. Still, the FSU coach made clear just how significant those decisions can become when they arrive in the biggest moments.

"Some of those moments can be game changers," Norvell said . "They can be life changers."

That comment carries added weight after how Florida State's 43-35 double-overtime loss at Miami ended.

With FSU trailing by eight and facing fourth-and-21 in the second overtime, quarterback Ashton Daniels found Micahi Danzy in the end zone for what initially appeared to be a 36-yard touchdown. Left tackle Xavier Chaplin was flagged for holding, wiping out the score and moving the Seminoles back to fourth-and-31. FSU still would have needed a two-point conversion to tie the game.

Daniels' final desperation throw was then ruled an interception by Miami safety Bryce Fitzgerald after he and Duce Robinson came down with the ball in the end zone. Replay upheld the ruling, ending the game.

Norvell was far more pointed about the holding penalty immediately after reviewing the game, calling it an "absolute joke" and confirming that Florida State had submitted the play to Patterson and the ACC for review.

After speaking with Patterson again, Norvell emphasized the process behind those conversations. Coaches submit plays they have questions about each week, both to receive clarification for their own players and to give the conference an opportunity to evaluate its officials.

"There's going to be good calls; there are going to be bad calls," Norvell said. "Sometimes there are just misses, and that's where he's able to teach his officials on things that they see or what they think they see."

Norvell did not publicly reveal what Patterson told him about the Chaplin penalty, saying their discussion would remain between them. Instead, he stressed the stakes attached to decisions made in moments that can alter games, seasons, and potentially much more.

The controversial ending will not change Florida State's record. The Seminoles remain 3-4 entering their matchup with Clemson, and Norvell acknowledged that controversial calls are ultimately something teams have to accept, learn from, and move past.

articles.title: Los estados de ánimo de Lamine tras el Balón de Oro: pasó de la decepción a la seguridad de que lo ganará
articles.standfirst: El extremo, pese a creer que lo conquistaría, encajó bien que lo levantara Kane
articles.summary: El extremo, pese a creer que lo conquistaría, encajó bien que lo levantara Kane
articles.body: Lamine Yamal no conquistó ayer lunes el Balón de Oro. El Trofeo que, cada año otorga la revista francesa especializada France Football, como mejor jugador del mundo recayó en Harry Kane. El extremo culé, de 19 años, creía realmente en sus opciones de levantar el preciado galardón, pero pese a la decepción, el joven internacional no baja los brazos y muestra una gran madurez: está seguro de que lo acabará ganando. Un tanto frustrado. Así se sintió Lamine en los primeros instantes tras conocer que había quedado en tercera posición en la clasificación del Balón de Oro 2026, por detrás de Kylian Mbappé y de Harry Kane, el ganador. El canterano culé realmente pensaba que su rendimiento, juego y títulos le convertían en un claro favorito a recibir el prestigioso premio. Titular indiscutible en el Barça y uno de sus máximos goleadores (el curso pasado intervino en 45 encuentros y marcó 24 goles - lideró el Zarra junto a Ferran Torres- y este ya suma 10 dianas en 13 cruces), ganó el Mundial el pasado verano con España y LaLiga y la Supercopa con el Barça, además de desplegar un fútbol vistoso, creativo, explosivo y vertical y ser un jugador desequilibrante y diferencial. Así mismo, destaca por tener una gran personalidad, que le ha convertido, pese a su juventud, en uno de los capitanes del Barça. Pero el vencedor fue Kane. Lamine, que ganó el Trofeo Kopa por tercer año consecutivo, accedió al pódium, quedó por delante de su compañero Rodri, que fue cuarto, y de Leo Messi, que finalmente quedó en quinta posición. Fue un revés que le llega justo tras la derrota en el Clásico. Una decepción más. Tiene 19 años, pero su talento hacía que muchos, no sólo él, creyeran que lo podía ganar. Los máximos representantes de la entidad, con Joan Laporta a la cabeza, y la mayoría de sus compañeros de vestuario también le veían favorito. Y esa confianza le acabó de convencer de sus opciones de ganar el Balón de Oro. No fue así. Pese a la frustración inicial, Lamine acabó encajando bien quedar en tercera posición. No se hundió. No se detuvo en lamentaciones o en reproches. Quería ganarlo y se veía con serias opciones de conquistar el Trofeo. Pero no levantarlo no frena su ambición. Es joven y está seguro de que si se mantiene en la línea actual volverá a estar nominado y lo acabará conquistando. Y cree que lo conseguirá más pronto que tarde. Desde el Barcelona aplauden la actitud de su joven estrella mundial y comparten sus emociones: de la decepción inicial, Laporta pasó a estar seguro de que la relación del extremo derecho con el Balón de Oro sólo es un 'hasta pronto'. Están muy orgullosos de él, en todos los sentidos. El presidente azulgrana, además, acabó muy satisfecho de la gala, donde el Barça arrasó en la mayoría de los premios. Fueron distinguidos, además de Lamine con el Kopa, Pere Romeu, Alexia Putellas, Vicky López, Cata Coll y Pere Romeu...

articles.title: Los jugadores de la AE Prat tienen un premio extra si eliminan al Athletic en la Copa del Rey
articles.standfirst: El restaurante Gastro Garatx invitará a todo el equipo a un menú degustación
articles.summary: El restaurante Gastro Garatx invitará a todo el equipo a un menú degustación
articles.body: La Copa del Rey está en marcha. El torneo del K.O. es una de las competiciones preferidas de muchos clubs, sobre todo los más modestos, que ven en este torneo una gran posibilidad de lograr victorias legendarias, hacer caja y entrar en la historia con triunfos inesperados ante entidades de mayor categoría. Esta semana muchos clubs de Primera entran en competición. Uno de ellos es el Athletic. El conjunto vasco se mide, en esta primera ronda, a la AE Prat, y los jugadores del bloque del Baix Llobregat tendrán un premio extra si eliminan a los de San Mamés. Los responsables y cocineros del restaurante Gastro Garatxe, Eric Ochoa y Carlos Novo, invitarán a todos los futbolistas de la AE Prat a un menú degustación si el próximo jueves eliminan al Athletic en la Copa del Rey. "Vosotros dadlo todo en el campo, que nosotros ya estamos pensando en el menú", comentan. "Que el Athletic tiene mucha historia, sí... pero nosotros tenemos hambre de sorpresa", insisten. "La propuesta está sobre la mesa", aseveran divertidos en sus redes sociales. Gastro Garatxe es un restaurante muy conocido en toda la zona que fusiona la cocina de autor y creativa con la tradicional desde el cuidado de los productos, en su mayoría de proximidad. Ha recibido diferentes distinciones por su calidad, innovación y servicio. El encuentro entre la AE Prat y el Athletic se disputa el próximo jueves a las 21.00 horas en el Municipal de L'Hospitalet. Toda la localidad del Baix Llobregat confía en que su equipo dé la campanada y elimine al bloque de Terzic. Los futbolistas, que militan en la Liga Élite Catalana, ya saben que además de seguir en la Copa del Rey podrán disfrutar de un gran ágape si vencen al conjunto vasco.

articles.title: Pérez Llorca señala a Peter Lim: "El problema del Valencia es Peter Lim, no que haya más o menos inversores"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la Generalitat carga contra el máximo accionista del Valencia al valorar la entrada del fondo de inversión americano en el club de Mestalla
articles.summary: El presidente de la Generalitat carga contra el máximo accionista del Valencia al valorar la entrada del fondo de inversión americano en el club de Mestalla
articles.body: El presidente de la Generalitat Valencia, Juan Francisco Pérez Llorca, ha cargado duro contra la figura de Peter Lim, todavía máximo accionista del Valencia pese a la venta de un importante porcentaje de su paquete accionarial al fondo de inversión americano Pitchwise que ha entrado en la propiedad con fuerza y pretende darle un giro al Valencia. El presidente de la Comunitat, que ha participado en el Ciclo regional de 20minutos, 'El pulso de nuestras Comunidades', y se ha sincerado con respecto a la situación del Valencia y el nuevo reparto accionarial. "He leído las noticias de que hay un fondo de inversión que va a aportar dinero al Valencia y bienvenido sea. Yo creo que el problema del Valencia es Peter Lim, no que haya más o menos inversores, sobre todo porque un club de fútbol en este país como es el Valencia no es solo una empresa. Si tú te lo tomas como una empresa de dividendos y encima estás a miles de kilómetros, en Singapur, yo creo que no entiendes la cultura de vivir y ver el fútbol", ha asegurado Pérez Llorca. El presidente hizo una comparativa con el club de baloncesto de la ciudad gestionado por Juan Roig para dejar clara su postura. "Si encima tienes la suerte de estar en una capital que tiene otro deporte que está triunfando, como es el baloncesto y todos vemos que el propietario de ese club no se lo toma como un tema empresarial, se lo toma como un tema de sentimiento. Ves la comparativa y te das cuenta de que el señor Lim no ha entendido lo que es el Valencia. Bienvenidos sean los nuevos inversores, ojalá mejoren las condiciones económicas, pero yo creo que el problema lo tiene el presidente del club, que no ha entendido lo que es el Valencia".

articles.title: Week 9 college football odds, storylines: Best bets for Florida-Georgia and Saturday's other big games
articles.summary: Matt Russell gives bets he likes on the biggest games of college football Week 9, including Florida-Georgia.
articles.body:
Call it a cherry pick on a week where it suits our narrative, but it sure seemed like line moves took it on the chin more than usual, and almost exclusively, in the highest-profile games of Week 8 of college football:

Indiana: Went up to -7.5, didn't cover the close at Michigan

Auburn: Went down to +7, didn't cover vs. LSU

Texas Tech: Went up to -11.5, lost outright at Cincinnati

Oregon: Went up to -10.5, lost outright to Illinois

Iowa: Went up to -7.5, lost outright to Minnesota

BYU: Went up to -7.5, lost outright to UCF

Ole Miss: Went down to +3, didn't cover the close at Texas

With BYU dropping a wild one at Central Florida (not completely unforeseeable given the obvious through-line of what the "spot" means in this emotionally-driven sport), market moves are inevitable, but who's to even say what a shake-up even is in college football anymore?

Texas saved its season with a win over Ole Miss, further complicating everything in the SEC, before many of the jumbled top-half of the conference take Halloween off. After Georgia (+100 to win the conference), which is no lock to make it to Atlanta given the Bulldogs have three more ranked games on their schedule, no one else is shorter than 7-to-1 odds.

In the Big Ten, Indiana exuded something at The Big House that so many of these teams aren't able to after a big game: upset avoidance. Meanwhile, Iowa and USC ejected themselves from the conversation out of the Big Ten, leaving just UCLA (-130) and Northwestern (+600) as the surprise teams looking to make a case for a third playoff team out of the conference we've been told is now the best in the sport.

The big one in the Group-of-Six was the slobber-knocker we expected between New Mexico and North Dakota State (the under kept us 2-2 in Week 8, 21-17-2 on the season). New Mexico jumped into the driver's seat for the Mountain West's top team, as the Lobos hope the other G6 conference leaders continue to drop.

In that vein, the upsets started early in Week 8, as James Madison got upset by Appalachian State on Thursday, removing the Dukes from the playoff equation as they went from odds-on to 10-to-1 to make it.

Middle Tennessee, Illinois, Southern Miss, Cincinnati, West Virginia and Louisiana-Monroe all deserve a shoutout for winning as underdogs of 3-to-1 on the moneyline.

A week after the Big 12's big day thanks to BYU, the Knights and Bearcats had no problem stinging the top of the league, as both the Cougars and Red Raiders move to plus-money to make the College Football Playoff.

The Rebels' loss didn't just move them to even-money to make the CFP, it dinged Trinidad Chambliss' chances for the Heisman Trophy in the betting market, as he fell to 30-1, while Miami's duo of Darian Mensah (+290) and Malachi Toney (+370) stacked stats in a game the Hurricanes were three-touchdown favorites. The countdown is on, as it's two weeks until they go to South Bend to take on the fourth choice in Heisman betting, CJ Carr (19-1). The winner coming out of that game will be a mover in a market still led by Jeremiah Smith (+120).

This is the space for the big games of the week. While we'll never get a true sample size in a sport that comes down to a bounce or two and the micro-assessment of replay reviews, the season's started to take shape. That said, there's enough market reaction (or lack thereof) to lead us to one side or another for the best games of Week 9.

No. 22 Arizona at No. 13 Texas Tech (-3.5, 54.5)

When Halloween lands on a game day, the ghosts of Michael Crabtree (the concept, not the very-much alive person) permeate through Lubbock on the anniversary of the Red Raiders' biggest win, back in 2007.

Luckily for Arizona, this one is not being played after dark for the Wildcats' second chance at getting noticed on a national level, having only lost at BYU.

Entering Week 9, we have to wonder what remains of preseason priors, because a line of -3.5 suggests these two teams are just about equal on a neutral field, a far cry from a projected 16-point line in favor of Texas Tech before the season.

Let's take a look at each side's EPA/Play:

Texas Tech: offense: 0.08, defense: -0.06

And now their Success Rate on standard downs:

Texas Tech: offense: 51.9%, defense: 41.1%

Both metrics give the edge to the Wildcats, and, in looking at their lone common opponent — not apples-to-apples because Arizona played Cincinnati at home — the Wildcats blew out the Bearcats.

Finally, Arizona went shot-for-shot with BYU in Provo, at a time when the Cougars were at full strength with LJ Martin at tailback, and their continuity from 2025 gave BYU more of an advantage than if they played later in the season.

Louisiana Tech (-5.5, 57.5) at South Alabama

With Louisiana's upset loss to ULM, we'll make a pronouncement: The winner of this game will represent the Sun Belt West in the conference championship game.

That's enough to make it a big game by our measurements, especially for those holding Louisiana Tech (13-to-1) futures.

These two match up well in offensive metrics, but the quarterback position provides a fork in the road of this handicap.

The Jaguars had their starting QB Bishop Davenport for the first two games of the season, but haven't since, and aren't expected to this week. Meanwhile, Louisiana Tech's numbers are somewhat depressed by being without Blake Baker (72.2% compeltions, 10-1 TD:INT ratio) for two games, but he's back and the Bulldogs offense is at full bore.

Plus, the Bulldogs are also coming in off of back-to-back shutouts (over ULM and Old Dominion), while South Alabama's defensive metrics lag behind considerably.

Utah won, and pulled off a "bad-beat" win for Utes backers, in a slugfest against Houston last week, which came with the big national pregame show in town.

The Utes are right in the eye of the "spot" hurricane as they go on the road against an unranked team that's shown it's fully capable of knocking off a conference contender. Utah's last-minute cover of a touchdown spread might dissuade the betting market from downgrading a Utes offense that was almost entirely Devon Dampier on the run, and a defense that leaned on the blitz button.

The Bearcats are coming off their own big win — the upset over Texas Tech — but a 13-point win with 255 rushing yards that was never in doubt after halftime doesn't feel like it was a completely draining experience.

A weird game in Tucson followed by getting dragged into a shootout with West Virginia has kept Cincinnati's market rating down, but if you can manhandle the Red Raiders, you probably deserve a boost — and anything of the sort gets this line closer to Utah -3 than -6.

No. 17 Florida vs. No. 3 Georgia (-11.5, 56.5)

The nickname has changed, and now the location has too.

The rivalry matchup that used to be called, "the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party" in Jacksonville, is being played in Atlanta this time around, due to the ongoing renovations in Duval County. While that's not technically a home game for the Bulldogs, Georgia's certainly familiar with the Mercedes-Benz Stadium, having played at least one game there in every season since 2021.

Both sides had a midseason bye to prepare, but while Florida comes in off an upset win at Texas, Kirby Smart's side has been hearing his angry voice for two weeks after blowing a 14-0 lead at home in a loss to Auburn.

Those two results have tweaked a betting line that we had projected at -12.5 prior to Week 7, as Florida's play-level finally found its level after a hot start. However, the postgame win expectancy for the Bulldogs was 96.7% per ESPN's Bill Connelly, and just 16.3% for Florida, suggesting both results were something of a fluke.
